# Chroma library earth: for Emren's review

Every situation offers all five colors, and every life stage is color-even on its own (see the checks file). Colors in brackets are how the act is tagged: one color, a combination named after its Magic group, or one color's means for another color's end. 'Leaves' is what the act writes into the person's history for later echoes to find. Values are Schwartz's ten, judged from the act itself.

## Everyday moments and life events, by stage

### a performance review

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · mixed · life: work · with: boss, colleague

Modern Earth: the yearly review with your manager, and a form that asks you to rate yourself first.

In words: Most employed adults, once a year; formal yearly reviews are the norm in offices and larger firms, less so in small or manual work (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{N} has a meeting with {boss} on Thursday, and a form that asks {N} to score the year from one to five.* (any color)  
> *The review form has twelve boxes, and {N} means to fill in every one honestly, the way the company asks.* (White)  
> *{N} reads the review criteria twice, looking for what is actually measured and what is only said.* (Blue)  
> *Raises are decided in these meetings, and {colleague} has already booked a long lunch with {boss}.* (Black)  
> *An hour of sitting across from {boss} talking about strengths and weaknesses. {N} already wants to scream.* (Red)  
> *It is the fourth review at the same desk. Outside the meeting room the leaves are turning, and {N} wonders how much of a year fits on a form.* (Green)  

- **fill in the self-assessment honestly, weak spots included** (White; works 60% of the time; value: conformity; leaves: owned up)
- **bring a page of figures showing exactly what your work achieved** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: achievement)
- **name the raise you want before your boss can name a lower one** (Black; works 69% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **tell your boss plainly what is wrong with how the team is run** (Red; works 58% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: defied an authority)
- **hear the feedback out without arguing, and keep to the work you are good at** (Green; works 90% of the time; value: tradition (humility))
- **put in a formal request to work four days a week and be home more** (White means, Green end; works 50% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **propose clear, fair criteria for reviewing the whole team** (Blue means, White end; works 45% of the time; value: universalism; says who you are)
- **flatter your boss into giving you the project you would learn most from** (Black means, Blue end; works 71% of the time; value: self-direction, achievement)
- **threaten, in the heat of the meeting, to walk out unless they promote you** (Red means, Black end; works 30% of the time; value: power)
- **take the middling score in your stride and keep your evenings for what you love** (Green means, Red end; works 82% of the time; value: hedonism)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {boss} nods along, and the form goes upstairs with a good word written on it. / The meeting ends early, with a handshake and a better number than {N} expected.  
If it fails: The meeting runs long, and the phrase "area for development" comes up four times. / The rating lands a point lower than last year, and nobody can say quite why.

### a neighbour's dog keeps you awake

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · trouble · life: home, conflict · with: a neighbour, partner

Modern Earth: the dog next door barks half the night, every night.

In words: About 1 in 3 adults, once or twice in a life, usually after a move; barking dogs are a common cause of neighbour noise complaints (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *For the third night running the dog next door barks from midnight until two, and {N} lies staring at the ceiling.* (any color)  
> *There are rules about noise after eleven, and the dog next door breaks them every night. The council's number is on the fridge.* (White)  
> *The barking starts at ten past twelve and stops at ten to two, almost to the minute. {N} begins to wonder what sets it off.* (Blue)  
> *{N} has an early meeting, and the dog next door has other plans. Somebody is going to pay for this lost sleep.* (Black)  
> *At two in the morning the dog is still at it, and {N} is out of bed in the dark with clenched fists.* (Red)  
> *The dog next door is left alone in the yard all night, howling like its wild cousins. {N} hears loneliness in it.* (Green)  

- **log the times and report the noise to the council** (White; works 40% of the time; value: conformity, security)
- **try earplugs, a fan and heavy curtains until something works** (Blue; works 85% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **hint to the neighbours that the landlord might hear about their other habits** (Black; works 62% of the time; value: power; closed by approval: a threat; backfire: a feud over the fence; leaves: made an enemy)
- **bang on their door at two in the morning and have it out** (Red; works 48% of the time; value: none clear (anger let out); closed by approval: a scene in the street; backfire: the police are called; body: light)
- **get to know the neighbours properly, and sort it out between you as friends** (Green; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, security; opens new ways)
- **quote the tenancy rules to their landlord until the dog has to go** (White means, Black end; works 20% of the time; value: power, security; closed by approval: getting a family's dog taken away; backfire: the street turns against you)
- **record the barking and turn it into a ridiculous song for the street's group chat** (Blue means, Red end; works 40% of the time; value: stimulation; closed by approval: mocking the neighbours in front of the whole street; backfire: the neighbours take offence, and the feud is on)
- **pay the neighbours' teenager to walk the dog every evening so it sleeps** (Black means, Green end; works 79% of the time; value: universalism (nature), security)
- **march round in the morning and make them promise the dog sleeps indoors** (Red means, White end; works 75% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **sit out in the yard at night, listening, until you understand what frightens it** (Green means, Blue end; works 35% of the time; value: self-direction, universalism (nature))
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The barking stops, or {N} stops hearing it, and sleep comes back. / By the end of the week the street is quiet after midnight.  
If it fails: The dog barks on, and now the neighbours no longer say hello. / A complaint arrives in the post, about the noise {N} made.

### a rival at work

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · trouble · life: work · with: rival, boss, colleague

Modern Earth: a colleague who started the same month keeps getting the projects you wanted.

In words: Most working adults, every few years, with a new job or a new team (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{rival} started the same month as {N}, and has somehow ended up with every project {N} wanted.* (any color)  
> *{rival} cuts corners and takes the credit, and {N} has watched the rules bend for them all year.* (White)  
> *{N} has been studying {rival} for months: the emails sent at seven in the morning, the way they speak in meetings.* (Blue)  
> *There is one promotion this spring, and only {N} and {rival} are in the running.* (Black)  
> *{rival} smirks across the meeting table, and {N} feels the heat rise to their face.* (Red)  
> *Two people with the same gifts in the same small team, {N} thinks; one of them was always going to have to grow somewhere else.* (Green)  

- **report your rival anonymously for every rule they bend** (White; works 35% of the time; value: conformity; closed by approval: an anonymous report; backfire: traced back to you, and trust lost)
- **study what your rival does well, and learn to do it better** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: achievement; leaves: learned a skill)
- **let slip, at the right moment, a mistake your rival made last spring** (Black; works 49% of the time; value: power; closed by approval: backstabbing; backfire: it gets back to them; leaves: made an enemy)
- **tell your rival to their face that you see exactly what they are doing** (Red; works 58% of the time; value: none clear (honesty of feeling))
- **ask to move to a team where your gifts fit better** (Green; works 65% of the time; value: security, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **ask for a formal mentor, so you grow on merit and not on politics** (White means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: achievement, self-direction; opens new ways; leaves: learned a skill)
- **read your rival's emails whenever they leave their screen unlocked** (Blue means, Black end; works 45% of the time; value: power; closed by approval: snooping on a colleague's account; backfire: caught, and a disciplinary hearing; builds habit)
- **line up a better offer elsewhere and leave with a flourish** (Black means, Red end; works 68% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; opens new ways)
- **challenge your rival to a game of squash and let it settle there** (Red means, Green end; works 68% of the time; value: stimulation, benevolence; body: light)
- **keep doing your share without complaint, so the team holds together** (Green means, White end; works 55% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By spring {N} is the one people come to, and {rival} knows it. / The tension eases, and the work starts going to whoever does it best.  
If it fails: {rival} gets the promotion, and the corridor feels longer every morning. / Word gets around, and {N} is the one who looks petty.

### a child's birthday party in the family

adult, ages 24 to 55 · everyday · joy · life: family · with: partner, parent, sibling, the birthday child, other parents

Modern Earth: the youngest in the family turns six, your own child or a niece or nephew, and the party is at your house.

In words: Most parents, once a year while their children are small, and a niece's or nephew's now and then (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The youngest in the family turns six on Saturday, the party is at {Ns} house, and twelve small guests are coming.* (any color)  
> *{N} has the list: twelve invitations and twelve party bags, so that no child in the class is left out.* (White)  
> *{N} has spent a week designing a treasure hunt whose clues get harder as the afternoon goes on.* (Blue)  
> *Last month {rival} hired a magician for a party just like this one. {N} has no intention of being outdone.* (Black)  
> *Balloons on the ceiling, music far too loud, and the birthday child running in circles, shrieking with joy.* (Red)  
> *{N} bakes the same lemon cake {parent} baked for every birthday, and the kitchen smells of childhood.* (Green)  

- **invite the whole class so that no child is left out** (White; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, universalism)
- **design a treasure hunt with clues for every age** (Blue; works 82% of the time; value: benevolence, self-direction)
- **hire the most impressive entertainer in town, and let the other parents see it** (Black; works 90% of the time; value: power (face); says who you are)
- **turn the music up loud and dance with the children till they drop** (Red; works 92% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; body: light)
- **bake the cake that was baked for every birthday of your own childhood** (Green; works 88% of the time; value: tradition; builds habit)
- **draw up a timetable of games so the fun never stops** (White means, Red end; works 78% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation)
- **hand out magnifying glasses and send the children on a bug hunt outside** (Blue means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: universalism (nature))
- **put the pushiest parent in charge of the games, so they cannot criticise** (Black means, White end; works 78% of the time; value: security)
- **let the children build a fizzing volcano in the garden and see what happens** (Red means, Blue end; works 88% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction)
- **invite only the families worth knowing, as your own parents always did** (Green means, Black end; works 40% of the time; value: power (face), tradition; closed by approval: snubbing the rest of the class; backfire: the excluded families talk)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The cake arrives whole, and the birthday child falls asleep on the sofa with icing on one cheek. / The children leave happy, and two parents ask for the recipe.  
If it fails: Two guests cry, one is sick, and the cake slides off the plate. / Half the class does not come, and the birthday child notices.

### a big night out after years of routine

adult, ages 26 to 55 · everyday · joy · life: leisure, friends · with: friend, partner, old friends

Modern Earth: an old friend's fortieth in a club in town, the first time the old crowd has met in years.

In words: Most adults, every few years, at a friend's round birthday, a wedding or a reunion (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{friend} is turning forty, the old crowd is meeting for the first time in years, and the babysitter is booked until two.* (any color)  
> *{N} promised {partner} to be home by two, and to keep an eye on {friend}, who never knows when to stop.* (White)  
> *{N} has not been out dancing in six years, and wonders with real curiosity what has changed out there.* (Blue)  
> *Half the guests are people {N} has wanted to meet for years, and the drinks are on {friend}.* (Black)  
> *The music hits {N} the moment the door opens, and six years of early nights fall away.* (Red)  
> *The old crowd is all here, greyer and softer, laughing the same laughs as twenty years ago.* (Green)  

- **stay sober so everyone gets home safe, as you promised** (White; works 92% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity; leaves: kept your word)
- **watch the crowd and work out how a night out has changed** (Blue; works 82% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **spend the night working the room and collecting useful numbers** (Black; works 85% of the time; value: power, achievement; builds habit, opens new ways)
- **dance until the lights come on and forget what time it is** (Red; works 92% of the time; value: hedonism; body: light; builds habit)
- **step outside with your oldest friend and talk under the night sky** (Green; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; leaves: made a friend)
- **give the birthday toast yourself, and make sure the room remembers who gave it** (White means, Black end; works 75% of the time; value: power (face))
- **plan the perfect route: three bars, a band, and a late-night food stall** (Blue means, Red end; works 55% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation)
- **slip the bouncer some cash so the whole old crowd gets in together** (Black means, Green end; works 82% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **make a sudden, heartfelt speech that brings the old crowd back together** (Red means, White end; works 78% of the time; value: benevolence; says who you are)
- **sit at the bar and hear out a stranger's whole life story** (Green means, Blue end; works 78% of the time; value: universalism, self-direction; opens new ways)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {N} gets home at dawn, hoarse and happy, with a story for every year of routine. / The old crowd swear to do it again next month, and this time they mean it.  
If it fails: The morning after is brutal, and so is the bank statement. / Something said at two in the morning is still being repeated a week later.

### the house needs repairs

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · trouble · life: home · with: partner, a roofer, a neighbour, parent

Modern Earth: a damp patch on the ceiling, and the roofer says it is worse than it looks.

In words: Most homeowners, a big unexpected repair every few years; about 2 in 3 US homes are lived in by their owners (US Census); the repair spacing is an estimate; likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *A damp patch is spreading across the bedroom ceiling, and the roofer says it is worse than it looks.* (any color)  
> *The roof is {Ns} responsibility now, and so is everyone who sleeps under it.* (White)  
> *{N} climbs into the loft with a torch to trace exactly where the water is getting in.* (Blue)  
> *The roofer's quote is three times what {N} expected, and {N} suspects someone is being taken for a ride.* (Black)  
> *Water drips into a bucket by the bed all night, tap, tap, tap, and {N} has had enough.* (Red)  
> *The house is a hundred years old, and every winter it lets in a little more of the weather, the way old houses do.* (Green)  

- **get three proper quotes and hire a certified roofer** (White; works 75% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **learn to fix the roof from manuals and videos, and do it properly** (Blue; works 45% of the time; value: self-direction; body: heavy; leaves: learned a skill)
- **beat the roofer down by inventing a cheaper quote from a rival** (Black; works 62% of the time; value: power (resources))
- **climb up in the rain tonight and patch it yourself** (Red; works 38% of the time; value: stimulation; body: heavy; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **call the old builder your family has always used, and do what he says** (Green; works 65% of the time; value: tradition; closed by law: the old builder is not certified; backfire: the insurer will not pay)
- **put a little aside every month to look after the old house** (White means, Green end; works 55% of the time; value: security, tradition; builds habit)
- **draw up a repair plan for the whole house, room by room, with a budget** (Blue means, White end; works 75% of the time; value: security)
- **offer the roofer cash in hand if he teaches you how it is done** (Black means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: learned a skill; told as: offer the roofer cash in hand if he teaches them how it is done)
- **rip out the old ceiling in one furious weekend and save thousands** (Red means, Black end; works 35% of the time; value: power (resources); body: heavy)
- **let the old house be imperfect, and spend the money on a summer by the sea** (Green means, Red end; works 20% of the time; value: hedonism)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The ceiling dries, and the house feels sound again. / The job comes in under budget, and the bedroom stays dry through the storms.  
If it fails: The leak moves two feet to the left and keeps dripping. / The repair costs twice the quote, and the damp is back by spring.

### a weekend with nothing planned

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · joy · life: leisure · with: partner, child, friend

Modern Earth: the calendar is empty from Friday night to Monday morning, for the first time in months.

In words: Most adults, a few times a year; parents of young children far less often (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *For the first time in months the calendar is empty from Friday night to Monday morning.* (any color)  
> *An empty weekend, and the list of jobs {N} promised to get round to is a long one.* (White)  
> *Two free days. {N} has a stack of half-read books and a question that has nagged for weeks.* (Blue)  
> *Two whole days when nobody needs anything from {N}. That time is worth something, and {N} means to spend it well.* (Black)  
> *Friday night, nothing planned, a full tank of petrol, and the road out of town is calling.* (Red)  
> *Saturday comes up slow and bright, the garden wet with dew, and nobody needs {N} anywhere.* (Green)  

- **work through the jobs you promised to do weeks ago** (White; works 80% of the time; value: conformity, benevolence; leaves: kept your word)
- **spend the weekend getting to the bottom of something you have always wondered about** (Blue; works 82% of the time; value: self-direction; opens new ways)
- **use the quiet days to get ahead on work nobody else is doing** (Black; works 88% of the time; value: achievement; builds habit)
- **head out of town with no destination and see where you end up** (Red; works 90% of the time; value: stimulation; opens new ways)
- **sleep late, potter in the garden and let the days unfold** (Green; works 93% of the time; value: hedonism)
- **sign up for the town's fun run you always meant to try** (White means, Red end; works 85% of the time; value: stimulation; body: light)
- **look up the old footpaths and find the spring your grandparents used to talk about** (Blue means, Green end; works 45% of the time; value: universalism (nature), tradition)
- **sell the clutter in the garage and give the takings to the school** (Black means, White end; works 78% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **take apart something broken on a whim, just to see if you can fix it** (Red means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation)
- **pick the apples in the abandoned orchard down the lane and keep them** (Green means, Black end; works 85% of the time; value: power (resources); closed by law: not your orchard; backfire: the owner turns up)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By Sunday evening {N} feels rested in a way no holiday quite manages. / The weekend turns up a small adventure that gets retold for years.  
If it fails: The weekend slips away in small chores and scrolling, and Monday comes too soon. / The plan goes wrong on Saturday morning, and the rest of the weekend goes with it.

### a budget that will not balance

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · trouble · life: money · with: partner, parent, the bank

Modern Earth: the mortgage went up, the childcare went up, and every month ends below zero.

In words: Many adults, a tight stretch every few years; about 1 in 3 US adults could not cover a $400 surprise bill with cash (Federal Reserve, 2023); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The mortgage has gone up, the childcare has gone up, and every month the account dips below zero before payday.* (any color)  
> *{N} has never missed a bill in their life, and does not mean to start now.* (White)  
> *{N} opens a spreadsheet and starts sorting a year of bank statements into columns.* (Blue)  
> *Somewhere in this mess money is leaking away, and {N} means to find it and keep it.* (Black)  
> *Another brown envelope on the doormat. {N} wants to tear it in half and go out for dinner anyway.* (Red)  
> *{Ns} grandparents raised five children on one wage and a vegetable patch. {N} keeps thinking about that.* (Green)  

- **cut every treat until the bills are paid, and stick to it** (White; works 60% of the time; value: security, conformity; builds habit)
- **track every purchase for three months and find the leaks** (Blue; works 62% of the time; value: security, self-direction; builds habit)
- **move the debt to a new card with a teaser rate and keep spending** (Black; works 40% of the time; value: power (resources); binds you)
- **stop opening the bills for a while and live a little** (Red; works 10% of the time; value: hedonism; builds habit)
- **dig a vegetable patch and cook from what it gives** (Green; works 22% of the time; value: security, tradition; builds habit)
- **sign up for the bank's free money course and do every exercise** (White means, Blue end; works 50% of the time; value: self-direction, conformity; leaves: learned a skill)
- **find every tax credit and allowance the rules permit, and claim them all** (Blue means, Black end; works 65% of the time; value: power (resources), security)
- **borrow from your parents again, and book the holiday anyway** (Black means, Red end; works 45% of the time; value: hedonism; binds you)
- **sell the car on impulse and walk or cycle everywhere from now on** (Red means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: universalism (nature), security; builds habit)
- **ask the family to pool money, the way your grandparents' generation did** (Green means, White end; works 40% of the time; value: tradition, security; binds you)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By the third month the account stays above zero. / The numbers finally line up, and {N} sleeps through the night.  
If it fails: An unexpected bill arrives and undoes a month of work. / The overdraft grows, and so do the arguments about it.

### a holiday dinner with both families

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · mixed · life: family, tradition · with: partner, parent, in-laws, child

Modern Earth: the holidays, and for the first time your family and your partner's at one table.

In words: Many couples, every few years at the holidays, as the families take turns to host (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{N} and {partner} are hosting both families for the holiday dinner: fourteen people around a table built for eight.* (any color)  
> *There is a right order to these things: who carves, who says grace, who sits at the head. {N} has thought it all through.* (White)  
> *{N} has drawn the seating plan four times, working out who must never sit next to whom.* (Blue)  
> *{partner}'s father has never thought {N} quite good enough. Today, with everyone watching, that can change.* (Black)  
> *By the second glass, an uncle is already circling the old argument about politics, and {N} feels the evening start to tip.* (Red)  
> *Two families, two sets of customs: one side lights candles, the other sings. The children want both.* (Green)  

- **keep every custom of both families, in the proper order** (White; works 62% of the time; value: tradition, conformity)
- **seat everyone so the old feuds never share a corner of the table** (Blue; works 72% of the time; value: security)
- **spend the whole evening winning over your partner's father** (Black; works 55% of the time; value: power (face), achievement)
- **raise the old argument after the second drink and have it out properly** (Red; works 12% of the time; value: none clear (feeling let out); leaves: made an enemy)
- **cook your grandmother's dishes and let the food bring everyone together** (Green; works 72% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence)
- **start a new tradition: both families, the same table, every year** (White means, Green end; works 58% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; binds you)
- **brief your partner beforehand on every subject to steer away from** (Blue means, White end; works 75% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **keep the old aunts' glasses full and learn the family secrets nobody mentions** (Black means, Blue end; works 68% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **tell the whole table, loudly, whose house this is** (Red means, Black end; works 15% of the time; value: power)
- **march both families out after the meal for a walk and a game in the park** (Green means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: hedonism, benevolence; body: light)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The two families leave as one noisy crowd, already arguing about who hosts next year. / Someone from the other side asks for a recipe, and something thaws.  
If it fails: The old argument breaks out over dessert, and two people leave early. / {partner} and {N} do the washing-up in a bitter silence.

### someone at work flirts with you

adult, ages 24 to 60 · everyday · mixed · life: love, work · with: colleague, partner

Modern Earth: a colleague lingers at your desk, laughs at your jokes and suggests a drink after work.

In words: Most adults, every few years in a working life; about 1 in 3 US workers say they have had a workplace romance (SHRM 2023); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{colleague} has started lingering at {Ns} desk, laughing a little too long at {Ns} jokes, and has suggested a drink after work.* (any color)  
> *Everyone in the office knows about {partner}. Still, {colleague} keeps finding reasons to stop by.* (White)  
> *{N} notices every small signal {colleague} sends, and cannot stop turning them over like a puzzle.* (Blue)  
> *{colleague} sits close to the head of the department, and the attention is flattering in more ways than one.* (Black)  
> *Something jumps in {Ns} chest every time {colleague} walks in. It has been years since {N} felt that.* (Red)  
> *{N} goes home to {partner}, to the warm kitchen and the old familiar arguments, and thinks about {colleague} all evening anyway.* (Green)  

- **tell them kindly and clearly that you are not available** (White; works 92% of the time; value: conformity, benevolence; says who you are; leaves: kept your word)
- **keep a careful distance while you work out what is missing at home** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: security, self-direction)
- **flirt back, since it might do your career some good** (Black; works 45% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **start an affair with them** (Red; works 40% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; closed by approval: betraying your partner; backfire: found out, and the relationship in crisis; leaves: broke your word)
- **let the feeling pass, as feelings do, and stay where your roots are** (Green; works 72% of the time; value: tradition, security; leaves: turned down a chance)
- **report the flirting to the office first, to protect your own position** (White means, Black end; works 45% of the time; value: security, power; closed by approval: reporting a colleague to cover yourself; backfire: a counter-complaint)
- **arrange the work trips so the two of you are alone, and nobody notices** (Blue means, Red end; works 35% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; closed by approval: deceiving your partner; backfire: found out; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **mention the flirting at home, so your partner remembers what they have** (Black means, Green end; works 58% of the time; value: security)
- **confess the crush to your partner in a rush, so nothing is hidden** (Red means, White end; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity; leaves: owned up)
- **let the feeling run its course, and watch what it shows about your life** (Green means, Blue end; works 65% of the time; value: self-direction)
- *(do nothing)*

- **let one of the little ones share your secret spot, if they swear to stay quiet** (Black means, Green end; works 45% of the time; value: benevolence, power)
- **jump out on purpose, so the little one who keeps losing finally finds someone** (Red means, White end; works 92% of the time; value: benevolence)

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.02, 0.02, 0.01, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0; moved by: stress+.4 money-.3 community-.3 era+.2.
In words: once, sometimes twice: about 2.5 in 100 children and 2 in 100 teenagers a year see their parents part, and 1 in 100 young adults still at home (D46, estimate); more where parents never married, fewer in much of Europe. Point 12 (Emren 2026-10-05): once: parents part once; a second split (a step-parent) is rare and not told as this event.; likelier with money worries, family strife, a parent's drinking or addiction, very young or unmarried parents, a time when divorce is easy and common; rarer with enough money, a faith or a close community, a close and steady family, parents who married older.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{Ns} parents sit {N} down at the kitchen table, both with careful faces. They are separating, and it sounds as if they rehearsed the words.* (any color)  
> *{N} wants to know how it will work: which nights where, who pays for what, where the holidays go. If there is a plan, it can be lived with.* (White)  
> *{N} has heard the arguments through the floor for a year and has a fair idea of the reasons already. Now {N} wants the true version.* (Blue)  
> *Two houses means two sets of rules, and two parents who both feel guilty. {N} notices how much room that leaves.* (Black)  
> *{N} is too old to cry in front of them and too angry not to. The chair scrapes back hard across the floor.* (Red)  
> *That evening {grandparent} rings. Some things change, {grandparent} says, but a family is still a family.* (Green)  

- **keep to the agreed week between the two homes, and keep up at school** (White; works 78% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **ask each parent, on their own, for the real reasons, and compare the answers** (Blue; works 50% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **play your parents off against each other for money, freedom and a later curfew** (Black; works 65% of the time; value: power, hedonism; builds habit)
- **tell them both exactly what you think of them, and storm out** (Red; works 50% of the time; value: none clear (hurt let out))
- **move in with your grandparents for a while, away from both houses** (Green; works 65% of the time; value: security, tradition; closed by approval: breaking the agreed week; backfire: a row between the grown-ups, and the week enforced)
- **refuse to change schools or leave your friends, whatever the grown-ups decide** (Red-Green (Gruul); works 75% of the time; value: security, tradition; says who you are)
- **listen in on their phone calls, to know what is coming before anyone says** (Blue-Black (Dimir); works 75% of the time; value: security; closed by approval: eavesdropping; backfire: overhearing far more than is bearable; builds habit)
- **choose which parent to live with, and argue your case to both** (Blue-Red (Izzet); works 70% of the time; value: self-direction; says who you are)
- **get both parents to agree one set of rules, and hold them to it** (White-Black (Orzhov); works 45% of the time; value: security, power)
- **keep the peace at both houses, and keep how you feel to yourself** (White-Green (Selesnya); works 45% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: Slowly the two houses become two homes, and {N} has a toothbrush in each. / {Ns} parents are kinder to each other apart than they were together, and {N} can feel the difference.  
If it fails: {N} goes quiet at school, and the teacher calls home. / The Friday handovers are cold and tense, and {N} dreads every one.

### the family moves to a new town

child, juvenile, ages 12 to 17 · life event · mixed · life: home, friends · with: parent, sibling, friend, grandparent

Modern Earth: the family moves to a town you have only seen on a map.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.03, 0.03, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0; moved by: prosper+.3 community-.3 ties-.2 era+.2.
In words: about 10 in 100 children and 7 in 100 teenagers a year move home with their family, and about four in ten of those moves go to another town (D37, data and estimate); US moves are at a record low, about half the rate of the 1960s; likelier with a parent's new job, a split, renting, a growing economy, cheap and easy travel; rarer with owning the home, grandparents and family nearby, a close community, a family farm or business.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The house is full of boxes and the walls are bare. Tomorrow the van leaves for a town {N} has only ever seen on a map, and all of {Ns} friends are staying here.* (any color)  
> *{N} has a list of everyone to keep in touch with, and means to keep at it, not just for the first month.* (White)  
> *{N} has looked the new town up: its river, its schools, the late bus to the city. It might be interesting.* (Blue)  
> *In the new town nobody knows who {N} was. {N} can be anyone at all.* (Black)  
> *Nobody asked {N}. {N} is leaving friends, a team and a whole life behind, and is furious about it.* (Red)  
> *{N} walks past the old school, the park and the corner shop one last time, trying to fix each one in memory.* (Green)  

- **promise every friend you will keep in touch, and message them every week** (White; works 55% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **look up everything about the new town: the schools, the clubs, the buses** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction; opens new ways)
- **decide to reinvent yourself at the new school, as someone people look up to** (Black; works 55% of the time; value: power, self-direction; says who you are)
- **refuse to pack, and shut yourself in your room with the music up loud** (Red; works 40% of the time; value: none clear (hurt let out))
- **walk your old streets one last time, and promise yourself you will come back** (Green; works 65% of the time; value: tradition; binds you)
- **join a team or a club in the first week, to find your feet fast** (White-Blue-Red (Jeskai); works 78% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; opens new ways)
- **set up your new room with all your old things, just as it was** (White-Blue-Green (Bant); works 70% of the time; value: security, tradition)
- **stay close to your family and keep a low profile until you know who to trust** (White-Black-Green (Abzan); works 55% of the time; value: security)
- **work out who runs things at the new school, and get on their side fast** (Blue-Black-Red (Grixis); works 65% of the time; value: power, security)
- **square up to the first kid at the new school who tries to push you around** (Black-Red-Green (Jund); works 60% of the time; value: power; closed by approval: fighting; backfire: suspended in the first week, with a reputation; body: light; told as: square up to the first kid at the new school who tries to push them around)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: Within a month {N} has a new best friend and a favourite path to school. / The new town has a river, a library and a kid next door who is just as new.  
If it fails: {N} spends lunchtimes alone for weeks, and the old friends slowly stop replying. / {N} begs every night to go back, and nothing feels right for a long time.

### a friend's scam is paying well

young adult, adult, ages 18 to 40 · everyday · mixed · life: money, friends · with: friend, parent, the police, strangers online

Modern Earth: a friend is making good money selling festival tickets that do not exist, and offers you half to help.

In words: Uncommon: perhaps 1 in 15 young adults, once or twice (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{friend} turns the laptop round: nine hundred this week, from strangers buying festival tickets that do not exist. Half of it could be {Ns}, {friend} says, for running a few of the listings.* (any color)  
> *At the other end of every sale is someone who saved up for a weekend that will never happen. {N} keeps seeing the person, not the money.* (White)  
> *{N} sees exactly how it works, and exactly where it breaks: the bank that freezes an account, the one angry buyer who goes to the police.* (Blue)  
> *Nine hundred a week. {N} has done everything properly for years and has less to show for it than {friend} has after a month.* (Black)  
> *{friend} is laughing and flush and buying every round. The money is fast and loud, and part of {N} wants some of it.* (Red)  
> *{N} and {friend} go back to primary school. {N} does not want the money, and does not want to lose {friend} to this either.* (Green)  

- **post a warning about the fake listings, with your friend's name on it** (White; works 75% of the time; value: universalism, conformity; closed by approval: shaming a friend in public; backfire: the post spreads, and the friend's family turns on the poster; says who you are; leaves: made an enemy)
- **run the listings for a month, then get out before it unravels** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: achievement, power; closed by law: fraud; backfire: the bank freezes the account and passes the name to the police; leaves: broke the law)
- **turn it down, and start reselling real tickets at a fair markup** (Black; works 60% of the time; value: achievement, power; says who you are)
- **tell your friend it is disgusting, and walk out of the flat** (Red; works 75% of the time; value: universalism, self-direction; says who you are)
- **take a share for the family, and never ask where it came from** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence, security; closed by law: handling the proceeds of fraud; backfire: the police trace the money to the family's account; binds you; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **sit your friend down with their family, so the family can talk sense into them** (White means, Green end; works 55% of the time; value: benevolence, security)
- **save every listing, and send them all to the police without a name** (Blue means, White end; works 60% of the time; value: universalism, security)
- **ask to see how the money moves, and keep a copy, just in case** (Black means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: power, security)
- **say yes on the spot, and spend the first share that night** (Red means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: hedonism, power; closed by law: fraud; backfire: arrested when a buyer goes to the police; leaves: broke the law)
- **let it be: your friend lives how they like, and so do you** (Green means, Red end; works 60% of the time; value: self-direction)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: Whatever {N} chose, nothing comes back to {N}, and the summer goes on. / By the end of the summer the listings are gone, and {friend} is looking for real work.  
If it fails: A letter from the bank says {Ns} account is frozen while the police make enquiries. / {friend} hears what {N} did, and a friendship of twenty years ends in one phone call.

### a pub argument turns into a fight

adult, ages 25 to 50 · everyday · trouble · life: friends, conflict, body · with: friend, a barman, strangers

Modern Earth: an argument at the bar turns, and a man shoves your friend into the tables.

In words: Perhaps 1 in 3 adults who drink in pubs, once or twice (estimate); men far more often than women; likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *Somewhere between the third pint and the fourth, an argument about nothing turns. A man at the bar shoves {friend} into the tables, the glasses go over, and the whole pub goes quiet.* (any color)  
> *Even a pub on a Friday night has its rules, and the barman is already reaching for the phone. Someone needs to calm this before it becomes a matter for the police.* (White)  
> *{N} sees how it will go: the man is bigger and drunker than {friend}, his mate is circling behind, and the door is twelve steps away.* (Blue)  
> *{N} has a lot to lose: the job, a clean record, the mortgage application going in next week. Whatever happens in the next ten seconds must not land on {N}.* (Black)  
> *The shove lands on {friend}, and {N} feels it like a shove of {Ns} own. {Ns} fists are tight before any thought arrives.* (Red)  
> *{friend} has stood by {N} for twenty years. Nobody puts hands on {friend} while {N} is standing there.* (Green)  

- **step between them with your hands up, and tell them both to stop** (White; works 65% of the time; value: security, benevolence; body: heavy)
- **catch your friend's eye, nod at the door, and leave together** (Blue; works 65% of the time; value: security)
- **keep out of it, and make sure the barman sees you had no part** (Black; works 75% of the time; value: security, power; builds self-control; leaves: refused someone in need)
- **hit him, hard, before he can swing again** (Red; works 50% of the time; value: power, security; closed by law: assault; backfire: arrested and charged; body: heavy; leaves: hurt someone badly)
- **wade in and drag your friend out by the collar** (Green; works 55% of the time; value: benevolence; body: heavy; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **sit them both down, and make each one say what started it** (White means, Blue end; works 50% of the time; value: security)
- **wait for your moment, then shove him off balance and get out** (Blue means, Black end; works 50% of the time; value: power, security; closed by law: assault; backfire: he falls badly, and the cameras saw it all; body: heavy; leaves: broke the law)
- **get his mate first, so it is two on one** (Black means, Red end; works 40% of the time; value: power, stimulation; closed by law: affray; backfire: both arrested, and the night on the local news; body: heavy; leaves: hurt someone badly)
- **roar at him to back off, loud enough to stop the whole pub** (Red means, Green end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **call the regulars over, and let the room calm him down** (Green means, White end; works 60% of the time; value: security, tradition)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The man is steered out into the night, and the pub goes back to its noise. / {N} and {friend} walk home under the streetlights, sore and laughing.  
If it fails: There is a brawl, a broken table, and a police van outside within ten minutes. / {N} wakes up with a split lip and a statement to give at the station.

### fiddling the books at work

adult, ages 25 to 50 · everyday · mixed · life: work, money · with: boss, colleague, partner

Modern Earth: the expense claims at work go through you, and you notice that nobody ever checks them.

In words: Uncommon: some office workers who handle claims, once or twice in a working life (estimate); expense schemes are about 1 in 10 workplace frauds (ACFE); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The expense claims go through {N} now, and {N} has noticed what nobody else seems to have: nobody checks them. A hundred here and two hundred there, and the books would still balance.* (any color)  
> *{boss} gave {N} the books because {N} was the honest one. That trust sits on the desk like a paperweight.* (White)  
> *{N} can see the gap in the system as clearly as a missing tooth: one signature, never checked, and an audit only every three years.* (Blue)  
> *{N} has given this firm years of unpaid overtime. A few hundred a month would only be taking back what is owed.* (Black)  
> *The pay is poor and the days are long, and for one giddy afternoon the thought of getting away with something is the most alive {N} has felt in years.* (Red)  
> *Times are tight at home, and the bills come faster than the pay. The firm would never feel it; the household would.* (Green)  

- **go back through every colleague's old claims and report each slip** (White; works 70% of the time; value: conformity; closed by approval: turning on colleagues; backfire: the office freezes the reporter out, and a friend loses their job; leaves: made an enemy)
- **put through one small claim, just to see whether anyone notices** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction; closed by law: false accounting; backfire: flagged at the audit, and every claim checked; wears self-control down; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **take the gap to the boss, and ask for a raise for finding it** (Black; works 60% of the time; value: achievement, power)
- **hand in your notice, and go and find work that does not bore you** (Red; works 55% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; told as: hand in their notice, and go and find work that does not bore them)
- **take home the spare office supplies, as everyone always has** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: tradition; closed by law: theft from an employer; backfire: a new manager counts the stock, and a warning goes on file; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **ask, through the proper channels, for the overtime you are owed** (White means, Black end; works 50% of the time; value: achievement, conformity)
- **use what you know of the books to go freelance, and be your own boss** (Blue means, Red end; works 45% of the time; value: self-direction; says who you are)
- **take just enough to cover the bills at home, and mean to pay it back** (Black means, Green end; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, security; closed by law: theft from an employer; backfire: found at the year-end, and the job gone; wears self-control down; leaves: broke the law)
- **blurt out in the meeting that nobody ever checks the claims** (Red means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: universalism, conformity; leaves: defied an authority)
- **sleep on it for a week, and see whether the urge passes** (Green means, Blue end; works 50% of the time; value: self-direction; builds self-control)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The year-end comes and goes, and {N} sleeps well. / A month later things at work have changed, and {N} is glad of the change.  
If it fails: The auditors arrive early, and they ask for {N} by name. / {boss} calls {N} in, closes the door, and puts a file on the desk.

### the neighbour's van across your drive

adult, mature, ages 25 to 75 · everyday · trouble · life: home, conflict · with: a neighbour, partner, the council, the police

Modern Earth: for the third time this week the neighbour's van is parked across your drive, and you cannot get out.

In words: Many households, once every few years, often with a new neighbour (estimate); parking tops the causes of neighbour disputes in British surveys; likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *For the third morning this week the neighbour's van is parked across {Ns} drive, and {N} is going to be late for work again.* (any color)  
> *Blocking a driveway is against the rules, and {N} has looked up exactly which rule. The neighbour must know it too.* (White)  
> *{N} has started keeping track: Mondays and Thursdays, always after eleven at night, always when the neighbour's brother comes to stay.* (Blue)  
> *The neighbour seems to have decided that {N} is the sort who will put up with it. {N} would like to show him otherwise.* (Black)  
> *{N} stands on the step in work clothes, keys in hand, and feels the heat climb up {Ns} neck.* (Red)  
> *A street works when people rub along. {N} has seen feuds over less run for twenty years and outlast everyone's patience.* (Green)  

- **have the van towed away yourself, since he is breaking the rules** (White; works 60% of the time; value: conformity, power; closed by law: moving another person's vehicle; backfire: the towing bill and a police caution land on the one who called it; leaves: broke the law; told as: have the van towed away themselves, since he is breaking the rules)
- **photograph it each time, and send the neighbour a polite, dated list** (Blue; works 65% of the time; value: security; builds habit)
- **find out who his landlord is, and have a quiet word** (Black; works 65% of the time; value: power)
- **lean on the horn at seven in the morning until he comes out** (Red; works 55% of the time; value: self-direction; closed by approval: waking the whole street; backfire: the neighbours take his side)
- **knock with two coffees, and ask whether all is well at his house** (Green; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **ask the council to paint a line across your drive, and get your mornings back** (White means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: self-direction, conformity)
- **find out why he parks there, and suggest a swap that suits both houses** (Blue means, Green end; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, security; binds you)
- **tell him you know his van is untaxed, and you will report it** (Black means, White end; works 60% of the time; value: power, conformity)
- **go round tonight and ask him straight why he does it** (Red means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **put big planters along the kerb, so nobody can park there again** (Green means, Black end; works 65% of the time; value: power, security; closed by law: blocking the pavement; backfire: the council orders them removed, with a fine; leaves: defied an authority)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The van moves to the other side of the road, and stays there. / A month later {N} and the neighbour nod to each other in the street, and the drive is clear.  
If it fails: The feud spreads to the whole street, and the police are called twice. / A long scratch appears along the side of {Ns} car one morning.

### an insurance claim for more than you lost

mature, elder, ages 40 to 85 · everyday · mixed · life: money, home · with: partner, sibling, a loss adjuster, neighbours

Modern Earth: after a break-in the insurance form asks what was taken, and nobody would know if the list were longer.

In words: Uncommon: perhaps 1 in 5 people claim for a break-in in later life, and some are tempted to pad it (estimate); about 13 in 1,000 US households are burgled a year (BJS 2023); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The burglars took a laptop and a little jewellery. The insurance form has twelve empty lines, and the loss adjuster said on the phone that receipts help but are not essential.* (any color)  
> *{N} has paid the premium every month for twenty-six years without a single claim. The form asks for the truth and nothing more, and there is a box to sign at the bottom.* (White)  
> *{N} reads the policy twice and knows exactly what it covers, what it does not, and how the company checks.* (Blue)  
> *Twenty-six years of premiums, and now the company will try to pay as little as it can. {N} can see who comes out ahead if nobody pushes back.* (Black)  
> *{N} feels sick every time they walk into the bedroom where the drawers were tipped out. Somebody owes {N} for that feeling, and the form is all there is.* (Red)  
> *One of the rings was {Ns} grandmother's. No form has a line for what that was worth.* (Green)  

- **list exactly what was taken, nothing more, and sign it** (White; works 70% of the time; value: conformity)
- **read the policy line by line, and claim every penny it truly covers** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: security, achievement)
- **haggle with the adjuster over every item until the offer is fair** (Black; works 70% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **ring the insurer and tell them exactly what this has done to you** (Red; works 65% of the time; value: self-direction; told as: ring the insurer and tell them exactly what this has done to them)
- **claim little, and let the things go; the ring was never about money** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: tradition (accepting what is))
- **photograph and list everything you own from now on, room by room** (White means, Blue end; works 65% of the time; value: security; builds habit)
- **add a watch that nobody could ever prove you did not own** (Blue means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: power (resources); closed by law: insurance fraud; backfire: the adjuster checks, the claim is refused, and the police are told; leaves: broke the law; told as: add a watch that nobody could ever prove they did not own)
- **push the adjuster for a fast payout, and spend it on a holiday** (Black means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: hedonism, power)
- **value the ring at what it meant to you, not what it cost** (Red means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: tradition; closed by law: an inflated claim; backfire: the valuation is checked, and the whole claim stalls; leaves: hid a wrong; told as: value the ring at what it meant to them, not what it cost)
- **claim the way the neighbours did, with a little extra, as everyone does** (Green means, White end; works 60% of the time; value: conformity, tradition; closed by law: insurance fraud; backfire: the insurer looks hard at the whole street's claims; wears self-control down; leaves: gave in to pressure)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The payout arrives within the month, and the matter is closed. / {N} buys a new lock and a new laptop, and the house starts to feel like home again.  
If it fails: The insurer sends an investigator, who asks a great many questions. / The claim drags on for half a year, and the payout is a fraction of the loss.

### the first night in a cell

juvenile, young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 16 to 85 · everyday · trouble · life: conflict, body · with: parent, a custody officer, a solicitor

Modern Earth: a steel door shuts, the hatch slides closed, and the first night in a cell begins.

In words: Once, on the first night after an arrest that brings a record; 3 to 4 in 10 Americans are arrested by 23, mostly for minor things (Brame 2012), far fewer held overnight; likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The door shuts with a sound {N} will remember for years. A thin mattress, a hatch in the door, a light that never goes off, and a whole night ahead.* (any color)  
> *{N} broke the law, and the law has answered. There is a strange order to it: the forms, the times, the officer who checks the hatch every hour.* (White)  
> *{N} lies on the mattress and goes over it again and again: every choice that led here, and which one, if any, could have gone the other way.* (Blue)  
> *{N} is already thinking about tomorrow: the solicitor, the story, who knows what, and how to come out of this with as little lost as possible.* (Black)  
> *The walls are too close. {N} paces, three steps and turn, three steps and turn, with a shout sitting just under the ribs.* (Red)  
> *Somewhere out there the family will have heard by now. {N} thinks of the kitchen at home and the light left on over the back door.* (Green)  

- **ask the officer for the rules, and keep every one of them** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity, security)
- **go over the whole thing, step by step, and find where it turned** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **work out what to say tomorrow that gets you home soonest** (Black; works 75% of the time; value: power, security; told as: work out what to say tomorrow that gets them home soonest)
- **kick the door and shout until someone comes** (Red; works 45% of the time; value: self-direction; closed by approval: kicking off in custody; backfire: a longer stay, and another charge; body: light; leaves: defied an authority)
- **lie still, breathe slowly, and let the night pass the way nights do** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: tradition (accepting what is), security)
- **ask for the phone call you are allowed, and ring home** (White means, Green end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity; told as: ask for the phone call they are allowed, and ring home)
- **ask for the duty solicitor, and learn exactly what you face** (Blue means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **chat to the officer at the hatch, and find out what they know** (Black means, Blue end; works 65% of the time; value: security, power)
- **swear to yourself that nobody will ever lock you up again** (Red means, Black end; works 95% of the time; value: power, self-direction; told as: swear to themselves that nobody will ever lock them up again)
- **hum the songs from home under your breath, to keep yourself together** (Green means, Red end; works 70% of the time; value: tradition; builds habit; told as: hum the songs from home under their breath, to keep themselves together)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: Morning comes, and {N} walks out into the daylight steadier than when the door shut. / The night passes, and {N} even sleeps a little before the hatch opens on breakfast.  
If it fails: The night is endless, and by morning {N} is shaking with tiredness. / The night goes badly, and {N} comes out with more trouble than before.

### a friend asks you for an alibi

adult, mature, ages 25 to 65 · everyday · trouble · life: friends, conflict · with: friend, partner, the police

Modern Earth: the police are asking where your friend was on Saturday night, and your friend asks you to say they were with you.

In words: Rare: perhaps 1 in 20 adults, once (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{friend} rings late, voice low. The police are asking about Saturday night and a smashed shop window on the high street, and {friend} wants {N} to say they were together all evening.* (any color)  
> *Lying to the police is a crime of its own, {N} knows, and it would make {N} part of whatever {friend} did.* (White)  
> *{N} thinks it through: who else saw {friend} on Saturday, which phones were where, how many places a story like that can come apart.* (Blue)  
> *{friend} would owe {N} for this, properly owe, for years. That is worth something. So is staying out of it.* (Black)  
> *{N} hears the fear in {friend}'s voice and wants to say yes before the sentence is finished.* (Red)  
> *{friend} has been family to {N} for thirty years: weddings, funerals, the bad winter. Families stand together; that is what {N} was always taught.* (Green)  

- **ring the police yourself, before your friend can ask anyone else** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity, security; closed by approval: turning in a friend; backfire: the friend's family never speaks to the caller again; leaves: made an enemy; told as: ring the police themselves, before their friend can ask anyone else)
- **say nothing either way yet, and keep every message they send** (Blue; works 80% of the time; value: security)
- **say yes, and make sure they know they owe you for life** (Black; works 60% of the time; value: power; closed by law: giving the police a false alibi; backfire: the story comes apart, and both are charged; binds you; leaves: broke the law; told as: say yes, and make sure the friend knows they owe them for life)
- **tell your friend straight to face it, and that you will go with them** (Red; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence; binds you; builds self-control)
- **say yes: you were together, as far as anyone needs to know** (Green; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; closed by law: giving the police a false alibi; backfire: a camera on the high street says otherwise, and both are charged; says who you are; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **tell the police the truth, and ask them to keep your name out of it** (White means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **help your friend put together a story that does not need you in it** (Blue means, Red end; works 50% of the time; value: benevolence; closed by law: helping to mislead the police; backfire: the story falls apart in the interview room; leaves: hid a wrong; told as: help their friend put together a story that does not need them in it)
- **find your friend a good solicitor, and pay for the first hour** (Black means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **tell your friend you love them, and that they must own up** (Red means, White end; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- **ask your friend round for a meal, and hear the whole story first** (Green means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The police lose interest, and {friend} rings to say it is over. / {friend} faces it in the end, and the friendship comes through.  
If it fails: An officer rings {N} to ask a few more questions about Saturday night. / {friend} hangs up, and does not ring again for a long, long time.

### learning to use a new phone

elder, ages 60 to 105 · everyday · mixed · life: era, everyday · with: child, grandchild, friend, a shop assistant

Modern Earth: your daughter gives you a smartphone and sets it up for video calls.

In words: Most older people, a new phone every few years; most Americans over 65 own a smartphone (Pew 2021: 61 in 100); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{child} has set up a new phone for {N}, all glass and no buttons, and it buzzes in {Ns} palm like a trapped bee.* (any color)  
> *{child} has written the steps on a card in neat capitals. {N} means to follow them in order, the way instructions are meant to be followed.* (White)  
> *The phone has a hundred settings and no printed manual. {N} puts on reading glasses and decides to understand every one of them.* (Blue)  
> *With this thing {N} could check the bank, the pension and the price of everything without asking anyone for help ever again.* (Black)  
> *A video of the grandchildren arrives with a ping, and {N} laughs out loud at the kitchen table and wants more of them.* (Red)  
> *{N} turns the phone over in hands that learned on a dial telephone, and wonders whether a life needs this at all.* (Green)  

- **go to the library's free class for older learners and do the homework** (White; works 85% of the time; value: conformity, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **work through every setting yourself, and quietly turn off anything that reports on you** (Blue; works 65% of the time; value: self-direction, security; closed by approval: the family's peace of mind; backfire: found out, and a row; leaves: hid a wrong; told as: work through every setting themselves, and quietly turn off anything that reports on them)
- **learn just enough to run your bank and pension without anyone looking over your shoulder** (Black; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction, power)
- **press everything, send odd messages to everyone, and laugh at the mistakes** (Red; works 55% of the time; value: stimulation, hedonism; opens new ways)
- **put it in the drawer and keep the old phone that still works** (Green; works 86% of the time; value: tradition)
- **take it to the shop and insist on the free help their advert promised** (White means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: power, security)
- **learn to film and send silly videos to the grandchildren** (Blue means, Red end; works 75% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction)
- **pretend you cannot learn it, so the children keep coming round to help** (Black means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: security, benevolence; builds habit)
- **join the street's group chat the very first evening, and greet everyone** (Red means, White end; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, universalism)
- **learn it slowly, one thing a week, the way you once learned to knit** (Green means, Blue end; works 80% of the time; value: self-direction)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By the end of the week {N} sends a photograph to {child} without any help. / The first video call works, and a small face fills the screen.  
If it fails: The phone locks itself after three wrong codes and stays locked. / {N} deletes all the contacts by accident and has to ask for help again.

### a fall at home

elder, ages 65 to 110 · everyday · trouble · life: body, home · with: child, neighbour, partner, a paramedic, a physiotherapist

Modern Earth: your foot catches the hall rug and you go down hard.

In words: About 1 in 4 people over 65 fall each year, and one fall doubles the chance of another (CDC); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{Ns} foot catches the hall rug, and suddenly the ceiling is very far away and the floor is very cold.* (any color)  
> *{N} lies on the hall floor reciting what the leaflet said to do after a fall: keep still, check for pain, call for help.* (White)  
> *From the floor {N} works out exactly what happened: the curled rug, the dim bulb, the reading glasses left upstairs.* (Blue)  
> *Flat on the floor, {Ns} first thought is that if {child} hears of this, the talk about moving will start all over again.* (Black)  
> *{N} is down on the hallway floor, furious at the rug, at the knee, at being old at all.* (Red)  
> *Lying on the cold tiles, {N} listens to the clock and the rain, and waits for the body to say what it can do.* (Green)  

- **phone for help at once, as you promised the family, and wait** (White; works 90% of the time; value: security, conformity; leaves: kept your word)
- **work out why you fell and make the house safe, room by room** (Blue; works 80% of the time; value: security, self-direction)
- **get up, clean up, and tell nobody, so nobody can say you cannot cope** (Black; works 58% of the time; value: power, self-direction; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **haul yourself up, swear at the rug and throw it out the back door** (Red; works 54% of the time; value: none clear (feeling let out); body: heavy)
- **lie still, breathe, and let your body tell you when it can move** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: security, tradition (accepting limits); told as: lie still, breathe, and wait until their body says it can move)
- **sign up for the clinic's balance class, so you can keep your garden** (White means, Green end; works 78% of the time; value: security, tradition; builds habit)
- **read up on falls and run a safety check for the neighbours too** (Blue means, White end; works 78% of the time; value: benevolence, universalism; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **hire a private physiotherapist and rebuild your strength by the numbers** (Black means, Blue end; works 80% of the time; value: achievement, security; body: light)
- **refuse the walking frame and keep walking to the shops alone** (Red means, Black end; works 53% of the time; value: self-direction, power; body: heavy)
- **walk in the park every morning until your legs and your freedom come back** (Green means, Red end; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; body: light; builds habit)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The bruise fades, and {N} is walking to the shops again within the month. / Nothing is broken, and the house is safer for it.  
If it fails: The hip is cracked, and the weeks in hospital are long. / {N} lies on the floor for hours before anyone comes.

### a scam phone call

elder, ages 60 to 105 · everyday · trouble · life: money · with: a stranger on the phone, child, friend, the bank

Modern Earth: a polite voice says it is your bank, and your savings must be moved tonight.

In words: Nearly every older person gets scam calls; a convincing one that names your bank comes every few years (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The phone rings at dinner. A calm voice says it is the bank's fraud team, and that {Ns} savings must be moved tonight.* (any color)  
> *The caller quotes a reference number and speaks for the bank. {N} was raised to trust people who speak for an institution.* (White)  
> *The caller knows {Ns} name and the last four digits of the card. {N} listens closely for the one thing that does not fit.* (Blue)  
> *Someone is trying to play {N} for a fool over the phone. {N} smiles at the kitchen wall: two can play at that.* (Black)  
> *The voice is so urgent that {Ns} heart starts racing. The money, the money, and no time to think.* (Red)  
> *{N} remembers when the bank was a man called by his first name behind a counter in {place}. This voice is nobody {N} knows.* (Green)  

- **hang up and ring the bank on the number printed on your card** (White; works 95% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **keep them talking and ask questions only the real bank could answer** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction, security)
- **pretend to fall for it and feed them a made-up account number** (Black; works 70% of the time; value: power, stimulation)
- **tell the caller exactly what you think of them and slam the phone down** (Red; works 92% of the time; value: none clear (feeling let out))
- **trust your gut, say you will sort it out at your branch, and hang up** (Green; works 92% of the time; value: security, tradition)
- **tape a rule by the phone, never talk money on a call, and stop dreading it** (White means, Red end; works 90% of the time; value: security, self-direction)
- **look the scam up and show your friends and family how it works** (Blue means, Green end; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **play along and set them up for the police to catch** (Black means, White end; works 18% of the time; value: universalism, stimulation; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **ring the number straight back to find out who on earth they are** (Red means, Blue end; works 20% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction)
- **draw your savings out and keep them at home in a tin, as your parents did** (Green means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: security, tradition)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The call ends, the money stays where it is, and {N} sleeps soundly. / The bank thanks {N} and blocks the number for good.  
If it fails: By morning, money is missing from the account. / {N} is shaken for weeks and jumps every time the phone rings.

- **dance with them in the kitchen to the songs your mother sang** (Red means, Green end; works 83% of the time; value: tradition, hedonism)

- **give a proper speech and thank every guest by name** (White; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- **ask each guest for one memory and write them all in a book** (Blue; works 90% of the time; value: self-direction, benevolence)

### the doctor says to stop driving

> *{N} has driven the lanes around {place} for fifty years and knows every bend by heart, if no longer by sight.* (Green)

- **learn the eye chart by heart before the retest** (Blue; works 40% of the time; value: self-direction; closed by law: cheating a medical test; backfire: caught, and the licence gone for good)

- **give the car to a young relative and walk wherever your legs allow** (Green; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; body: light)
- **petition the council for a bus stop at the end of your road** (White means, Black end; works 25% of the time; value: power, security)
- **learn the bus and train timetables, and plan trips beyond anywhere the car went** (Blue means, Red end; works 80% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **trade your car to the neighbour's son in return for weekly lifts** (Black means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: security, tradition; binds you)
- **rage about it, then throw yourself into the campaign for better buses** (Red means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: universalism, benevolence)
- **accept it, and use the slower days for the books you never had time for** (Green means, Blue end; works 78% of the time; value: self-direction; opens new ways)
- *(do nothing)*

If it fails: The house feels smaller every week without the car. / {N} misses {friend}'s birthday for want of a lift, and broods for days.

### sorting out your will

elder, ages 60 to 105 · everyday · mixed · life: money, family · with: a solicitor, child, sibling, grandchild, partner

Modern Earth: the solicitor writes that your will is twenty years out of date.

In words: About half of older people, once or twice; only about 1 in 3 US adults has a will at all (Caring.com survey 2024); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The old will is in a brown envelope from twenty years ago. Half the people in it have changed, and two of them have died.* (any color)  
> *{N} wants it fair, legal and properly witnessed, so that nobody can quarrel over it at the funeral.* (White)  
> *{N} spreads the accounts, the deeds and the policies across the dining table and draws the whole estate as a diagram.* (Blue)  
> *Everyone in the family will be a little kinder to {N} once they hear a will is being written. {N} knows that very well.* (Black)  
> *{N} cannot bear the thought of {child} and {sibling} fighting over the furniture when it is all over.* (Red)  
> *The ring was {Ns} grandmother's, and the clock came from the farm. Things should go where they belong.* (Green)  

- **divide everything fairly between your heirs, signed and witnessed properly** (White; works 88% of the time; value: universalism (fairness), conformity)
- **quietly move money between accounts so nobody can follow it** (Blue; works 60% of the time; value: security, power; closed by law: hiding assets from the tax office; backfire: an inquiry and frozen accounts)
- **let everyone in the family think they might get the most, and watch them** (Black; works 55% of the time; value: power)
- **give the treasured things away now, while you can see their faces** (Red; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, hedonism)
- **leave each heirloom to the one it belongs with, as your family always has** (Green; works 72% of the time; value: tradition)
- **write a formal letter of wishes: no mourning clothes, a party, and your favourite songs** (White means, Red end; works 94% of the time; value: hedonism, self-direction)
- **set up a careful trust so what came down to you stays in the family** (Blue means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: tradition, security; binds you; told as: set up a careful trust so what came down to them stays in the family)
- **hold off signing until everyone in the family is on speaking terms** (Black means, White end; works 40% of the time; value: benevolence, power)
- **follow your heart and leave the most to the young relative who longs to study** (Red means, Blue end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence, self-direction)
- **keep everything in your own name to the end; the young can wait their turn** (Green means, Black end; works 75% of the time; value: power, security)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The will is signed, witnessed and filed, and a weight lifts from {Ns} shoulders. / Over Sunday lunch the family takes the plan far better than {N} feared.  
If it fails: The papers sit unsigned on the sideboard for another year. / Word gets out, and {child} stops speaking to {sibling}.
