### the first months of retirement

mature, elder, ages 55 to 80 · life event · mixed · life: work, time · with: partner, friend, former colleague, child, grandchild

Modern Earth: the leaving party is over, and Monday morning has no alarm.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 2.0; moved by: money+.4 health+.3 prosper+.3 era+.2.
In words: once, for most people who stop work for good, in the first year after the last day at work: most people in rich countries retire between 60 and 70, on average at about 64 for men and 63 for women across the OECD (Pensions at a Glance 2023); the engine lets in only people who retired within the year, so the yearly figure is per new retiree (Library 22:40); likelier with money and a pension that pays enough, good health, a fixed pension age, a growing economy, a job that has changed past recognition; rarer with low money or no pension, poor health (which forces retirement instead), caring duties that already fill the days, work of one's own, a calling still loved.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The leaving card is on the mantelpiece and the alarm clock is unplugged. It is Monday morning, and nobody expects {N} anywhere.* (any color)  
> *For forty years {N} knew where to be at eight o'clock. Now the days need a shape, and {N} means to give them one.* (White)  
> *Time at last for every book, course and question {N} put off for forty years. {N} makes a list, and the list is long.* (Blue)  
> *{N} spent a career being someone people needed. The phone has gone quiet, and {N} has no intention of becoming nobody.* (Black)  
> *No boss, no commute, no meetings. {N} stands in the doorway in a dressing gown, grinning at the open week.* (Red)  
> *The garden needs digging, the grandchildren need collecting from school, and the season has turned. {N} lets it.* (Green)  

- **draw up a weekly timetable: volunteering Mondays, the pool Wednesdays, family Sundays** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity, security; builds habit)
- **enrol at the university for the degree you never had time to finish** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction, achievement; opens new ways, says who you are)
- **go back as a paid consultant, on your own terms and at twice the rate** (Black; works 68% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **buy an old camper van and just go** (Red; works 76% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **spend the mornings in the garden and the afternoons with family and friends** (Green; works 79% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; builds habit)
- **take the lump sum, buy a smallholding and live off the land** (Black-Green (Golgari); works 48% of the time; value: security, self-direction; opens new ways, binds you)
- **walk the woods and rivers every day and become the local expert on birds** (Blue-Green (Simic); works 70% of the time; value: universalism (nature), self-direction; leaves: learned a skill)
- **turn the garage into a workshop and invent things all day long** (Blue-Red (Izzet); works 75% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; builds habit)
- **take the chair of a charity board and run it like your old department** (White-Black (Orzhov); works 62% of the time; value: power, benevolence; says who you are)

If it works: By spring, {Ns} days are fuller than they ever were at work. / {N} sleeps well, laughs more, and stops checking the old work emails.  
If it fails: The days blur together, and {N} is still in a dressing gown at noon. / {N} misses the work and the people more than expected, and the house is very quiet.

### your partner dies

adult, mature, elder, ages 45 to 110 · life event · trouble · life: loss, partner · with: partner, child, sibling, friend, a priest

Modern Earth: after decades together, your husband or wife dies.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.002, 0.006, 0.04; moved by: harsh+.5 unrest+.3 money-.3 health-.3.
In words: once for most, rarely twice: per married person about 0.2 in 100 adults, 0.6 in 100 in midlife and 4 in 100 elders a year lose their partner (2 at 65-74, 5 at 75-84, 12 at 85 and over), women more often and earlier (D52, estimate from the SSA life table); likelier with an older partner, a husband (men die younger), poverty, smoking, a long illness already in the house, a harsh place, war; rarer with a younger partner, money, good health and good health care.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{partner} died in the night. The other side of the bed is cold, and the whole house seems to be listening.* (any color)  
> *There are forms, a funeral, a notice in the paper and people to ring in the right order. {N} does each one, because {partner} would have.* (White)  
> *{N} reads the death certificate again and again, the cause, the hour, as if the right reading could make sense of it.* (Blue)  
> *Fifty years of sharing everything, and now the money, the house and every decision rest on {Ns} shoulders alone.* (Black)  
> *The grief hits {N} like weather, all at once, and {N} howls into {partner}'s coat in the hall.* (Red)  
> *The roses {partner} planted are in bud. They will flower without {partner}, and somehow, so will {N}.* (Green)  

- **arrange the funeral exactly as you both agreed, and keep every custom** (White; works 68% of the time; value: tradition, conformity; leaves: kept your word)
- **read everything about grief and keep a journal of each day** (Blue; works 68% of the time; value: self-direction; builds habit)
- **take charge of the money and the house at once, and decide everything alone** (Black; works 76% of the time; value: self-direction, security; says who you are)
- **let yourself fall apart, and cry wherever and whenever it comes** (Red; works 77% of the time; value: none clear (grief let out))
- **keep their chair, their garden and their routines, as if they were still here** (Green; works 68% of the time; value: tradition; builds habit; leaves: stayed home)
- **sell up within the month and go somewhere neither of you ever went** (Black-Red (Rakdos); works 48% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways; leaves: moved away)
- **walk out to the hills you both loved and scatter the ashes yourself** (Red-Green (Gruul); works 70% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; body: heavy)
- **go through every one of their papers, looking for what they kept hidden** (Blue-Black (Dimir); works 64% of the time; value: security, self-direction)
- **let the family and old friends carry you through the first year** (White-Green (Selesnya); works 64% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; told as: let the family and old friends carry them through the first year)
- **join a bereavement group and follow its course week by week** (White-Blue (Azorius); works 72% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: In time {N} can say {partner}'s name and smile. / The first year passes, and {N} is still standing, and not alone.  
If it fails: {N} stops eating properly and barely leaves the house for months. / The family drifts away after the funeral, and the silence is enormous.

### moving to a smaller home or into care

mature, elder, ages 55 to 110 · life event · mixed · life: home · with: child, sibling, neighbour, an estate agent, the care home staff

Modern Earth: the stairs have become too much, and the family house goes on the market.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.01, 0.04; moved by: family-.4 health-.4 community-.3 prosper+.2.
In words: once or twice: about 1 in 100 a year in the late fifties and 4 in 100 elders downsize or move into care (D37, data and estimate: D37 counts any move, about 5 in 100 in midlife); moves into care rise steeply after 80; likelier with living alone, a divorce or a death in the house, renting, a fall or an illness, stairs, a house too big to keep up, family far away; rarer with a partner at home, family nearby, a close community, good health, an owned, paid-off house close to shops and doctors.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *Forty years of things in one house, and the new flat has two rooms. {N} stands in the attic with a roll of bin bags.* (any color)  
> *The family has agreed, the forms are signed, and the move is on the fourteenth. {N} labels every box with a date and a room.* (White)  
> *{N} has compared eleven places: their staff, their fees, their inspection reports, and how far each is from the library.* (Blue)  
> *The house is worth a fortune now. {N} means to get every penny of it and choose the next place without asking anyone's leave.* (Black)  
> *{N} cannot stand the thought of a beige room and a timetable, and the anger comes out at whoever is nearest.* (Red)  
> *This house is where {N} raised a family. Now it will raise someone else's. That is what houses are for.* (Green)  

- **move on the date the family agreed, with every box labelled** (White; works 70% of the time; value: conformity, security)
- **visit every place on the list and choose by the inspection reports** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: security, self-direction)
- **sell to the highest bidder and buy the best flat money can buy** (Black; works 78% of the time; value: power, security)
- **refuse to go, and dig in your heels for as long as you can stand** (Red; works 50% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **give the furniture to whoever will love it, and keep only the photographs** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; leaves: left home)
- **hold a farewell evening: a story for each room, then a dance in the empty one** (White-Blue-Red (Jeskai); works 90% of the time; value: hedonism, tradition)
- **choose a place in your own neighbourhood, with a garden, and move in slowly** (White-Blue-Green (Bant); works 70% of the time; value: tradition, security)
- **march into the care home office and get the best room in writing** (White-Black-Red (Mardu); works 58% of the time; value: power, security)
- **rent the house out, live on the income, and keep it in the family** (Blue-Black-Green (Sultai); works 65% of the time; value: security, tradition; binds you)
- **sell up and go back to the village you were born in, whatever anyone says** (Black-Red-Green (Jund); works 65% of the time; value: self-direction, tradition; says who you are; leaves: moved away)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The new place is light and warm, and {N} is surprised to love it. / The move goes smoothly, and the neighbours are friendly from the first day.  
If it fails: {N} cannot settle, and lies awake missing the old creaking stairs. / The move goes badly: boxes go missing, a treasured cabinet breaks, and tempers fray.

mature, elder, ages 55 to 105 · life event · joy · life: love · with: prospect, child, friend, grandchild

Modern Earth: at the dance class, the same person keeps choosing you as a partner.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.06, 0.03; moved by: ties+.5 health+.4 community+.3 money+.2.
In words: any time after fifty-five, sometimes more than once: per single, divorced or widowed person about 6 in 100 a year in midlife and 3 in 100 after sixty-five (D12, data and estimate, set per eligible person by the engine at pull-in, 06:29), lower for women; likelier with widowed or divorced for a while, good health, money, clubs, classes and a busy social life, a community to meet people in; rarer with poor health, raw grief, caring duties, grown children who object.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *At the Thursday dance class {prospect} keeps choosing {N} as a partner, and tonight asks about coffee afterwards.* (any color)  
> *{N} was married for decades and believed in forever. Is there a right and proper way to begin again at this age?* (White)  
> *{N} has not been courted since before mobile phones. There must be a way to read the signals, and {N} studies them.* (Blue)  
> *{prospect} is charming, comfortable and lonely. {N} is old enough to know exactly what is on offer, and what it is worth.* (Black)  
> *{Ns} heart is pounding like a teenager's, and {N} feels ridiculous, and does not care in the least.* (Red)  
> *{N} thought that part of life had closed, like a season. But here is spring, of all things, in the seventies.* (Green)  

- **invite them to Sunday lunch with the family, and court them properly** (White; works 65% of the time; value: tradition, conformity)
- **take it slowly, and get to know them over many long conversations** (Blue; works 68% of the time; value: self-direction, benevolence)
- **keep your money separate and your will unchanged before it gets serious** (Black; works 90% of the time; value: security, power)

- **trust your instinct about them, and let it unfold without plans** (Green; works 68% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **draw up a careful agreement on money and homes before moving in together** (White-Blue-Black (Esper); works 68% of the time; value: security; binds you)
- **marry them with the whole family there, and the youngest as attendants** (White-Red-Green (Naya); works 55% of the time; value: tradition, hedonism; says who you are, binds you)
- **keep your own homes, share your Sundays, and keep the family's blessing** (White-Black-Green (Abzan); works 78% of the time; value: security, tradition)
- **set off together on a long trip to places neither of you has seen** (Blue-Red-Green (Temur); works 70% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **carry on in secret, so the family never gets a say in it** (Blue-Black-Red (Grixis); works 72% of the time; value: self-direction, hedonism; closed by approval: the family; backfire: found out, and a family row; leaves: hid a wrong)

If it works: {N} is happier than in years, and does not hide it. / {child} meets {prospect}, and after an awkward first hour, likes them.  
If it fails: {child} is horrified, and the row lasts all summer. / It fizzles out after a few weeks, gently, and {N} is left a little lonelier.

### honoured for your life's work

mature, elder, ages 50 to 105 · life event · joy · life: community, work · with: mentor, colleague, friend, child, rival, the local paper

Modern Earth: a letter says you are to be honoured for a lifetime of work.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.01, 0.02; moved by: community+.5 ties+.3 money+.2 prosper+.2 unrest-.3 fortune+.1.
In words: once or twice in later life: about 1 in 100 a year in midlife and 2 in 100 elders are publicly honoured for a lifetime's work (estimate scaled down from D22, which counts any recognition); the big public honours reach fewer than 1 in 1,000; likelier with a long career in one place, years of volunteering, a public role, a craft the town knows by name, wide ties, money that makes the work seen; rarer with a quiet life, frequent moves, work nobody sees, low money, unrest, discrimination.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The letter is on heavy paper: {N} is to be honoured at a dinner for a lifetime's work. There will be a speech, and a photographer.* (any color)  
> *{N} reads the letter twice. It is an honour from the town {N} served for decades, and it should be received with dignity.* (White)  
> *The citation gets two dates wrong and misnames the first project. {N} reaches for a pen.* (Blue)  
> *At last the people who overlooked {N} for years will have to stand up and applaud.* (Black)  
> *{N} reads the letter and whoops out loud in the kitchen, then rings {friend} at once.* (Red)  
> *{N} thinks of {mentor}, who taught {N} the work, and of all the hands it passed through before and since.* (Green)  

- **accept graciously, wear your best, and thank the committee in a proper speech** (White; works 85% of the time; value: conformity, tradition)
- **rewrite the speech for weeks, until every word is exact** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: achievement, self-direction)
- **invite everyone who ever doubted you, and make sure they see it** (Black; works 75% of the time; value: power, achievement; says who you are; told as: invite everyone who ever doubted them, and make sure those people see it)
- **turn the dinner into a party, and dance with the mayor** (Red; works 75% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; body: light)
- **say it belongs to everyone you worked beside, and share the stage with them** (Green; works 82% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition (humility); says who you are)
- **use your new standing on the town's committees to steer money to your own causes** (White means, Black end; works 45% of the time; value: power; closed by approval: a conflict of interest; backfire: a scandal in the paper; says who you are)
- **write a frank, funny memoir of the work, mistakes and all** (Blue means, Red end; works 45% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; says who you are)
- **use your new fame to raise the money to save the old woodland** (Black means, Green end; works 50% of the time; value: universalism (nature), power)
- **use the speech to blast the council for cutting the very work you did** (Red means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: universalism; closed by approval: at an honours dinner; backfire: a cold room and no more invitations; says who you are)
- **spend the next year teaching an apprentice everything your hands know** (Green means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; binds you)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The applause goes on longer than anyone expected. / {Ns} photograph goes up in the town hall, and {child} keeps the cutting from the paper.  
If it fails: The evening is stiff and hollow, and {N} is glad when it is over. / {rival} gives a speech that steals the evening.

### facing the end

mature, elder, ages 50 to 110 · life event · trouble · life: body, meaning, faith · with: child, partner, friend, sibling, a doctor, a priest

Modern Earth: the doctor says the treatments have run out, and there may be a few months left.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.004, 0.035; moved by: health-.8 harsh+.4 stress+.2.
In words: once; most deaths in old age follow a known decline (estimate from life tables: a death risk of 1-2% a year at 60-70 and 5-9% at 80-85; Part D has no entry for one's own death); likelier with a serious illness, great age, poverty, smoking, a hard working life; rarer with good health, wealth, good care.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The doctor sits down, which doctors only do for one kind of news. A few months, perhaps; the treatments have run out.* (any color)  
> *There are things to put in order: the will, the funeral, the apologies and the thanks. {N} means to leave nothing undone.* (White)  
> *{N} asks for the scans, the numbers and the honest odds, and wants to understand exactly what is coming.* (Blue)  
> *{N} has beaten long odds before. There must be a trial, a specialist, a clinic abroad, some door nobody has tried.* (Black)  
> *Months, then. {N} intends to live every one of them at full volume.* (Red)  
> *The leaves are turning outside the hospital window. {N} watches them fall and feels, strangely, part of it.* (Green)  

- **call the family in one by one, and say what must be said** (White; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; leaves: owned up)
- **ask for every result, and read until you understand your illness** (Blue; works 62% of the time; value: self-direction, security)
- **demand the best specialists, and pay for every scan and trial there is** (Black; works 45% of the time; value: power, security)
- **leave the hospital, cash in the savings and do everything on the list** (Red; works 71% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation)
- **go home to die among your own things, with the window open** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: tradition (acceptance))
- **talk with the chaplain or a counsellor, and make your peace with what comes** (White means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: tradition)
- **write a clear plan for your care and your funeral, so nobody has to guess** (Blue means, White end; works 88% of the time; value: security, benevolence)
- **leave your body to the medical school, so even your death teaches something** (Black means, Blue end; works 92% of the time; value: universalism)
- **say every hard truth you held back for years; there is nothing left to lose** (Red means, Black end; works 62% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: made an enemy)
- **go back to the water you swam in as a child, and swim once more** (Green means, Red end; works 50% of the time; value: stimulation, tradition; closed by approval: the doctors; backfire: a collapse far from help; body: heavy; leaves: took a wild risk)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The last months are full of visitors, laughter and things said at last. / {N} finds a calm nobody expected, and shares it.  
If it fails: The pain is hard to manage, and the days are long and frightened. / Old quarrels are not mended in time, and {N} grieves for them.

### someone mocked for being different

juvenile, young adult, adult, mature, ages 11 to 67 · everyday · trouble · life: school, work, friends · with: rival, friend, colleague, a teacher or a manager

Modern Earth: a classmate or a colleague is mocked by the group for not acting the way a boy or a girl, a man or a woman, is supposed to.

In words: Most teenagers see it many times at school, adults now and then at work; GLSEN surveys find nearly all LGBTQ pupils in US schools hear such remarks (adult part an estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *In the corridor {rival} and two others trail a quiet member of the group, calling out the word they have used all month, and half the corridor laughs.* (any color)  
> *The rules on the noticeboard say nobody is to be picked on, and here it is happening right under them. {N} feels the duty to say something like a weight on the chest.* (White)  
> *{N} has watched it for weeks and seen the pattern: always the same three, always when nobody in charge is near, always the same word.* (Blue)  
> *{N} sees how it works: whoever stands next to the target becomes the next one. Keeping clear is the smart thing, and {N} hates how smart it is.* (Black)  
> *The laughter makes {Ns} face burn. {N} wants to shove through the crowd and tell {rival} where to go.* (Red)  
> *The one being mocked walks with eyes on the floor, the way a hurt animal moves. {N} remembers them on the first day, shy and hopeful, before everyone sorted themselves into groups.* (Green)  

- **report the name-calling to whoever is in charge, with the dates and the names** (White; works 70% of the time; value: universalism, conformity; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **ask them, away from everyone, what would actually help** (Blue; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **keep your distance, so the mocking does not turn on you** (Black; works 88% of the time; value: security; leaves: refused someone in need; told as: keep their distance, so the mocking does not turn on them)
- **step in front of them and tell the mockers to back off** (Red; works 75% of the time; value: universalism, stimulation; says who you are; leaves: made an enemy)
- **sit with them at lunch every day, as if nothing were odd** (Green; works 82% of the time; value: benevolence; builds habit, says who you are; leaves: made a friend)
- **ask whoever is in charge for a group talk where everyone can speak freely** (White means, Red end; works 80% of the time; value: universalism; opens new ways)
- **find out what they love, and bring them along to a club where it fits** (Blue means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence; leaves: made a friend)
- **warn the ringleader that a video exists and will reach the people in charge** (Black means, White end; works 62% of the time; value: power, universalism; closed by approval: threats; backfire: the video goes round, and the one being mocked is hurt again)
- **ask the mockers, loudly and in front of everyone, why it bothers them so much** (Red means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: universalism, stimulation)
- **laugh along with the rest, since that is how the pecking order works** (Green means, Black end; works 68% of the time; value: power, security; closed by approval: joining in the bullying; backfire: someone in charge hears, and there is trouble; wears self-control down; leaves: gave in to pressure)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By the end of the week the corridor is quieter, and {N} can live with the part played in it. / Things settle, and within a month the one being mocked walks a little taller.  
If it fails: The mocking goes on, and {N} feels sick about it every morning. / The mockers turn on {N} as well, and the next weeks are hard ones.

### your sibling brings home a same-sex partner

juvenile, young adult, adult, mature, ages 12 to 75 · everyday · mixed · life: family · with: sibling, parent, grandparent

Modern Earth: at the holiday meal a brother, a sister or a cousin brings home a partner of the same sex for the first time.

In words: About 1 in 4 people, once (estimate); about 9 in 100 US adults identify as LGBTQ+ (Gallup 2024), so many families have a brother, sister or cousin who will; likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{sibling} arrives for the holiday meal and, for the first time, brings a partner: someone of the same sex, holding flowers and a cake, smiling hard. Around the table the family goes very polite.* (any color)  
> *{N} was raised to welcome every guest at this table, and also on teachings that have hard words for this. Both are being tested before the soup.* (White)  
> *{N} watches the room: {parent}'s fixed smile, {grandparent}'s silence, the partner trying too hard. It is like a play where nobody has learned their lines.* (Blue)  
> *{N} sees at once that all the family's attention will be on {sibling} today. The usual questions about {Ns} own life will not come up, and that is not nothing.* (Black)  
> *{N} sees the partner's hands shaking round the cake tin and wants to do something, anything, to break the ice.* (Red)  
> *The family has gathered round this table for every holiday {N} can remember. Today it has one more chair, and the old table holds it.* (Green)  

- **lay a place for the partner, and treat them as any other guest** (White; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **ask the partner about their work and their life, and really listen** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: universalism; leaves: made a friend)
- **stay polite but distant, and keep your opinions to yourself** (Black; works 92% of the time; value: security)
- **raise a glass to the two of them before anyone can make it awkward** (Red; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, stimulation)
- **sit beside your grandparent and help them come round, slowly** (Green; works 62% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **refuse to sit at the same table, and let the family choose** (White means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: tradition, power; closed by approval: snubbing a guest at the family table; backfire: the family chooses, and not as hoped; says who you are)
- **start a quiz after dinner, so everyone has to talk and laugh together** (Blue means, Red end; works 75% of the time; value: hedonism, benevolence)
- **take your parent aside: accept this, or lose your sibling for good** (Black means, Green end; works 58% of the time; value: benevolence, power)
- **call out the uncle who makes a snide remark, right there at the table** (Red means, White end; works 70% of the time; value: universalism)
- **take the partner round the garden after lunch, and get to know them** (Green means, Blue end; works 88% of the time; value: benevolence; opens new ways; leaves: made a friend)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By the pudding the talk is easy, and the partner is laughing at the old family jokes. / {sibling} catches {Ns} eye across the table and mouths a silent thanks.  
If it fails: The meal limps to an early end, and {sibling} and the partner leave before the coffee. / Something said at the table is not forgotten, and the next holiday is thinner.

### the first person you tell

juvenile, young adult, adult, ages 14 to 45 · everyday · mixed · life: friends, love · with: friend, sibling

Modern Earth: after years of knowing, you tell one person, a close friend or a sibling, that you are gay or bisexual.

In words: Most gay and bisexual people, once; Pew 2013: LGB adults first told a close friend or family member at a median age of about 20, younger generations sooner; likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{N} and {friend} are sitting on the low wall outside the chip shop, as they have a hundred times, and {N} has decided that tonight is the night. The words are ready. The mouth is dry.* (any color)  
> *{N} has chosen {friend} with care: someone who keeps promises. {N} only hopes that {friend}'s ideas of right and wrong have room for this.* (White)  
> *{N} has rehearsed it a dozen ways and guessed {friend}'s answer to each. None of the guesses help now.* (Blue)  
> *{N} has weighed it up: {friend} is loyal, has secrets too, and has more to lose by telling than by keeping quiet. It is as safe a bet as {N} will get.* (Black)  
> *{Ns} heart is going like a drum. Either it comes out now or it stays in for good, and {N} cannot stand for good.* (Red)  
> *{N} has known {friend} since they were both small. If anyone in the world can take this as part of the same old {N}, it is {friend}.* (Green)  

- **ask your friend to promise to keep it secret, then tell them** (White; works 80% of the time; value: security; leaves: came out)
- **test the water first with a question about someone famous who came out** (Blue; works 82% of the time; value: security)
- **tell only the friend with a secret of their own to keep** (Black; works 82% of the time; value: security, power; leaves: came out)
- **just say it, straight out, before the nerve goes** (Red; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: came out)
- **wait for a quiet moment that feels right, and let it come out naturally** (Green; works 78% of the time; value: self-direction; says who you are; leaves: came out)
- **write it in a careful letter, so the words come out right** (White means, Blue end; works 80% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: came out)
- **say it is about someone else, and watch how your friend reacts** (Blue means, Black end; works 78% of the time; value: security; wears self-control down; leaves: kept it hidden)
- **wait for a night when your friend owes you one, then pour it all out** (Black means, Red end; works 78% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: came out; told as: wait for a night when the friend owes them one, then pour it all out)
- **blurt it out in tears, and let your friend hold you** (Red means, Green end; works 85% of the time; value: benevolence, security; gains friend for life; leaves: came out; told as: blurt it out in tears, and let the friend hold them)
- **decide not to tell anyone yet, and keep the peace a while longer** (Green means, White end; works 82% of the time; value: security, conformity; leaves: kept it hidden)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {friend} listens to the end, and then says the one thing {N} needed to hear. / The night goes on and the world has not ended; if anything it is bigger.  
If it fails: {friend} goes stiff and changes the subject, and the walk home is very quiet. / Within a week someone else knows, and {N} did not tell them.

### a love nobody can know about

juvenile, young adult, adult, ages 15 to 40 · everyday · mixed · life: love · with: prospect, friend, parent

Modern Earth: a first love with someone of your own sex, and nobody can know: not the family, not the school or the work, not the street.

In words: Many gay and bisexual people, once, in the teens or twenties, more often where it is condemned (estimate); hiding adds lasting stress (Meyer 2003); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{N} and {prospect} meet at the bus shelter at the far end of the park, where nobody they know ever goes. They hold hands for twenty minutes and let go the moment a car turns the corner.* (any color)  
> *{N} hates the lying: the invented evening class, the friend's house that is really the park. Honesty was always the first rule, and love has made {N} break it every week.* (White)  
> *{N} has built a whole system: separate chats, a nickname in the phone, routes home that never cross. It works, and it is exhausting.* (Blue)  
> *Nobody gets to take this. {N} guards the secret like money, and enjoys a little the power of a life nobody else knows about.* (Black)

### telling the family who you are

juvenile, young adult, adult, mature, ages 13 to 65 · life event · mixed · life: family, identity · with: parent, sibling, grandparent

Modern Earth: you tell your parents who you love, or who you are, and wait for what comes next.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.025, 0.035, 0.02, 0.01, 0.0; moved by: era+.5 ties+.2 prosper+.1 harsh-.4 unrest-.2 stress-.1.
In words: once, if ever: per person it concerns (attr >= 2, or gender unease) about 2 to 4 in 100 a year from the mid-teens into the thirties and fewer later, so that about two in three tell the family in a lifetime (estimate from Pew 2013: median first telling at about 20; about 6 in 10 LGB adults have told their mother and 4 in 10 their father, bisexual people far less often); younger generations tell sooner. Closes at 65, when most parents are gone; later tellings come through 'a late truth inside a marriage' and 'a name that has waited for decades'; likelier with a time and place where it is legal and spoken of; a family that has said kind things about people like this; a partner to bring home; a steady income or a home of one's own; friends who already know; rarer with a family faith or a community that condemns it; a country that punishes it; depending on the family for money or a roof; a family already in crisis.

> *{N} wants to do this properly: at home, at the table, with the whole family, the way important things have always been said. {N} only hopes the family's rules have room for the truth.* (White)  
> *{N} has thought it all through: who to tell first, the questions that will come, the leaflet folded in a pocket for {parent}. Nothing on paper says how a face will look.* (Blue)  
> *{N} has chosen the moment with care: after the job offer, with a place of {Ns} own lined up. Whatever the family says, nobody can take away the roof.* (Black)  
> *{N} is done with pretending at every birthday and every holiday. It is coming out today, whatever happens, and {Ns} hands are shaking.* (Red)  
> *{N} wants the family to know the whole of {N}, the way they have always known each other's joys and troubles. Belonging to them by halves is no longer enough.* (Green)  

- **tell them all together at the family table, calmly and with respect** (White; works 60% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; says who you are; leaves: came out)
- **tell them with answers ready, and meet every question with patience** (Blue; works 64% of the time; value: universalism; says who you are; leaves: came out)
- **wait until you no longer depend on them, then tell them on your own terms** (Black; works 62% of the time; value: self-direction, security; says who you are; builds self-control; leaves: came out)
- **say it at the big family party, out loud, and let the chips fall** (Red; works 60% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; leaves: came out)

- **tell them, and walk out for good if they will not accept it** (Black-Red (Rakdos); works 60% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: came out)
- **cry it out at the kitchen table, and ask for a hug** (Red-Green (Gruul); works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, security; leaves: came out)
- **ask a cousin who already knows to sit in when you tell them** (Blue-Green (Simic); works 65% of the time; value: security, benevolence; leaves: came out)
- **keep it from them for good, and keep the family as it is** (White-Black (Orzhov); works 75% of the time; value: security, conformity; leaves: kept it hidden)

### a long walk alone

juvenile, ages 12 to 18 · everyday · joy · life: nature, inner · with: parent, friend, a farmer, a stranger on the path

Modern Earth: a free day, and you set off walking alone, out of town, along the river and into the hills.

In words: About 1 in 3 teenagers, a few times a year (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{N} sets off alone with a bottle of water and no plan, out past the last houses and along the river toward the hills.* (any color)  
> *{N} told {parent} the route and the time to be back, and means to keep to both.* (White)  
> *Every bend of the path is a question: what that bird is, where the stream goes, how old the stone wall is.* (Blue)  
> *Out here nobody wants anything from {N}. It is the first chance in weeks to think about what {N} wants, and how to get it.* (Black)  
> *The wind hits {Ns} face at the top of the hill, and {N} breaks into a run for no reason at all.* (Red)  
> *The path is older than the town. {N} walks it slowly, listening to the river, and feels the noise of the week drain away.* (Green)  

- **keep to the route you promised, and be home exactly on time** (White; works 94% of the time; value: conformity, security; leaves: kept your word)
- **take a field guide and name every plant and bird you pass** (Blue; works 92% of the time; value: self-direction; opens new ways; leaves: learned a skill)
- **use the quiet to plan exactly how you will get what you want this year** (Black; works 92% of the time; value: achievement, power)
- **leave the path and scramble up to the highest point you can see** (Red; works 80% of the time; value: stimulation; body: heavy; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **sit by the river for an hour and do nothing at all** (Green; works 95% of the time; value: universalism (nature), hedonism)
- **promise yourself a long walk every Sunday, whatever else happens** (White means, Red end; works 55% of the time; value: hedonism, self-direction; builds habit)
- **map the old footpaths around your town and walk each one in turn** (Blue means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction, tradition; builds habit)
- **cut across the private farmland, so you are home exactly when you promised** (Black means, White end; works 80% of the time; value: conformity; closed by approval: trespass; backfire: chased off by the farmer, and home later than ever)
- **follow the stream on a whim, just to see where it goes** (Red means, Blue end; works 85% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **pick a bag of wild blackberries along the lanes and sell them to the neighbours** (Green means, Black end; works 50% of the time; value: achievement)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {N} comes home muddy, tired, and calmer than in weeks. / Somewhere on the hill, something {N} has been worrying about simply stops mattering.  
If it fails: Rain sets in, the path vanishes, and {N} gets home soaked and late. / {N} turns an ankle on the way down and limps the last mile.

In words: repeats, rarely: about 1.5 in 1,000 young adults, 3 in 1,000 adults and people in midlife, and 1.5 in 1,000 elders a year go bankrupt or sink under debts they cannot pay (D59 [data+est]: 533,949 US consumer bankruptcies in 2025, about 0.2 in 100 adults, peaking in middle age); the wider debt crises of 3 to 5 in 100 households a year come as a money squeeze, or as money running out at home in the teenage years; likelier with medical bills, a lost job, a divorce, gambling or addiction, a recession, unrest; rarer with money in the bank, health insurance, family who can help, a growing economy.

juvenile, young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 12 to 95 · life event · trouble · life: community, conflict · with: friend, rival, colleague, boss, parent, partner

- **face them all down, head up, and refuse to hide** (Red; works 68% of the time; value: self-direction; says who you are)

- **get someone everyone respects to vouch for you in public** (White means, Black end; works 52% of the time; value: power, security; told as: get someone everyone respects to vouch for them in public)
- **write your whole side of it, honestly and at length, where everyone can read it** (Blue means, Red end; works 45% of the time; value: self-direction; says who you are)
- **quietly call in favours until the group takes you back** (Black means, Green end; works 65% of the time; value: security, power; told as: quietly call in favours until the group takes them back)
- **go to each person you hurt, face to face, and say sorry** (Red means, White end; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence; leaves: owned up)

### two nights camping with friends by a lake

juvenile, young adult, ages 14 to 21 · everyday · joy · life: friends, nature, home · with: friend, parent, a campsite warden

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The tent goes up crooked on the third try, the stove hisses, the beans catch on the bottom of the pan, and the lake turns pink and then grey as {N} and {friend} sit in the doorway with nobody to tell them when to sleep.* (any color)  
> *{N} promised {parent} two things: a text every night at nine, and nobody in the lake after dark. {N} gave their word on both.* (White)  
> *{N} has the map, the forecast, three knots learned from videos and a checklist taped inside the lid of the food box. This trip will be done properly.* (Blue)

- **pitch the tent by the book, guy ropes pegged and a trench against the rain** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: achievement, security; leaves: learned a skill)
- **grab the best pitch by the water before the families arrive** (Black; works 80% of the time; value: power, security)
- **build a roaring fire on the shore, though the site bans fires** (Red; works 62% of the time; value: stimulation, hedonism; closed by approval: the campsite bans open fires; backfire: the warden puts it out and sends everyone home a day early)
- **drag your sleeping bag out of the tent and sleep under the open sky** (Green; works 88% of the time; value: universalism (nature))
- **ask the warden properly if the group may sit up by the fire past quiet hours** (White means, Red end; works 55% of the time; value: self-direction, conformity)
- **learn the stars from an app and name them for the others, one by one** (Blue means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: universalism (nature), self-direction)
- **trade your biscuits to the family next door for a lend of their gas** (Black means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: security)
- **set off round the lake at dawn with no map, to see the far side** (Red means, Blue end; works 82% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **catch a fish from the lake, cook it on the fire, and eat like kings** (Green means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: self-direction, hedonism; closed by law: fishing a private lake without a permit; backfire: the warden takes the rod and rings home; leaves: broke the law)

If it works: The tent holds through a night of rain, and in the morning the lake is as flat as glass. / They come home sunburnt, smoky and somehow two days older, with stories they will not tell their parents.

> *{N} has started watching the clock: the hour before the next pill is the worst. {N} knows what that pattern means.* (Blue)  
> *{N} knows which doctor at the practice signs repeat prescriptions without asking questions.* (Black)  
> *The pills take the edge off everything, not just the back. The week feels flat and grey without them.* (Red)  
> *The body heals in its own time. {grandparent} used to say that pain is a messenger, not an enemy.* (Green)  

- **finish the course as written, and hand the leftovers back at the pharmacy** (White; works 66% of the time; value: conformity, security; builds self-control)
- **keep a diary of the cravings, and come off them on a plan you draw up** (Blue; works 60% of the time; value: self-direction, security; builds habit; builds self-control)
- **order more from an online pharmacy that asks no questions** (Black; works 66% of the time; value: hedonism, security; closed by law: prescription drugs without a prescription; backfire: the pills are fakes; body: heavy; builds habit; wears self-control down; leaves: used drugs)
- **buy more from a friend of a friend when the bottle runs out** (Red; works 70% of the time; value: hedonism; closed by law: pills bought on the street; backfire: the pills are not what they seem; body: heavy; builds habit; wears self-control down; leaves: used drugs)
- **let the pain come back, and go out walking with it every morning** (Green; works 66% of the time; value: security, universalism (nature); body: light; builds habit; builds self-control)
- **bin the last pills, and go up into the hills to sweat it out** (Red-Green (Gruul); works 52% of the time; value: self-direction, universalism (nature); body: heavy; builds self-control)
- **tell the other doctor a well-rehearsed story, for a new prescription** (Blue-Black (Dimir); works 66% of the time; value: hedonism, security; closed by approval: lying to a doctor; backfire: the records are shared, and every prescription stops; wears self-control down; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **ask the physiotherapist about other ways to live with the pain** (Blue-Green (Simic); works 70% of the time; value: security, self-direction; opens new ways; leaves: learned a skill)
- **sign up for the clinic's programme quietly, so nobody at work finds out** (White-Black (Orzhov); works 58% of the time; value: security, achievement; binds you; builds self-control)
- **tell your partner or closest friend everything, and hand them the bottle** (White-Red (Boros); works 66% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity; binds you; leaves: owned up)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The last pill goes, the bad weeks pass, and {N} sleeps through a night again. / {N} comes off them slowly, and one morning notices that the clock has stopped mattering.  
If it fails: The bottle runs out on a Friday, and the weekend is the longest of {Ns} life. / By the spring the pills are part of every day, and {N} has stopped counting.

### a racing heart after a heavy weekend

adult, mature, elder, ages 35 to 90 · life event · trouble · life: body, health · with: a doctor, partner, friend, parent, child

Modern Earth: on the Monday after a heavy weekend your heart starts racing and stumbling, and the hospital asks how much you drink.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.002, 0.006, 0.008; moved by: stress+.4 health-.4 money-.1 trouble+.15.
In words: estimate: about 2 in 1,000 adults, 6 in 1,000 people in midlife and 8 in 1,000 elders a year end up in hospital with a racing or stumbling heart after heavy drinking (the "holiday heart" of Ettinger 1978); atrial fibrillation rises steeply with age, and each daily drink raises the risk by about 8 in 100 (Kodama 2011, Journal of the American College of Cardiology); likelier with heavy weekends, high blood pressure, stress, a family history, age; rarer with light drinking, fitness, a doctor seen regularly.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *On the Monday after a long weekend of drinking, {Ns} heart starts racing and stumbling like a bird against a window. By noon {N} is on a trolley with wires on their chest, and a young doctor is asking how much {N} drinks.* (any color)  
> *The doctor wants an honest number. {N} has always filled in forms truthfully, and the true number looks like a shock once it is written down.* (White)  
> *{N} watches the ragged trace on the monitor and wants to know exactly what is going on in there, and what the drink has to do with it.* (Blue)  
> *{N} knows the right number to give: low enough to sound sensible, high enough to be believed.* (Black)  
> *{N} is frightened, and furious at being frightened. Life without the weekends would hardly be life.* (Red)  
> *{parent} went the same way: a flushed face and a bad heart at sixty. {N} watches the screen and thinks of that.* (Green)  

- **give the doctor the true number, and sign up for the clinic** (White; works 64% of the time; value: conformity, security; builds habit; leaves: owned up)
- **read everything on the heart and drink, and set your own strict limits** (Blue; works 64% of the time; value: self-direction, security; builds habit; builds self-control; leaves: learned a skill)
- **give the doctor a lower number, and carry on as before at home** (Black; works 62% of the time; value: hedonism, security; builds habit; wears self-control down; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **discharge yourself, go to the pub, and drink to being alive** (Red; works 68% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; closed by approval: leaving against medical advice; backfire: the heart goes again, worse; wears self-control down; leaves: defied an authority)
- **stop drinking quietly, and spend the weekends out of doors instead** (Green; works 65% of the time; value: security, universalism (nature); builds self-control)
- **take on a dry year as a challenge, with a race at the end** (White-Blue-Red (Jeskai); works 50% of the time; value: achievement, stimulation; binds you; builds self-control)
- **follow the cardiologist's plan to the letter, with the best specialist money can buy** (White-Blue-Black (Esper); works 70% of the time; value: security, achievement; binds you; builds self-control)
- **tell the family, and agree a house rule: no drink in the house** (White-Black-Green (Abzan); works 60% of the time; value: security, tradition; builds self-control)
- **learn to cook properly, cycle to work, and let the body mend** (Blue-Red-Green (Temur); works 62% of the time; value: self-direction, security; body: light; builds habit)
- **decide that life is short, and keep the weekends exactly as they are** (Black-Red-Green (Jund); works 55% of the time; value: hedonism, tradition (acceptance); builds habit; wears self-control down; leaves: took a wild risk)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The heart settles into its old rhythm, and {N} goes home with a leaflet and a new resolve. / Six months on, the trace on the screen is steady, and the doctor says so.  
If it fails: Two weeks later the heart stumbles again, and this time the ambulance comes to the house. / The weekends go on as before, and the pill boxes on the kitchen shelf multiply.

### the cyclist at dusk

mature, elder, ages 60 to 100 · life event · trouble · life: body, freedom · with: child, partner, friend, a doctor, a stranger

Modern Earth: driving home at dusk, a cyclist appears at your bonnet out of nowhere, and you brake just in time.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.005, 0.02; moved by: health-.5 era+.1.
In words: estimate: about 5 in 1,000 drivers in their sixties and 2 in 100 elders who still drive a year have a near miss they come to blame on their eyes; drivers with cataracts have about two and a half times the crash rate (Owsley 1999), and cataract surgery cuts it by about half (Owsley 2002, JAMA); likelier with cataracts or macular disease, driving at dusk and in rain, a home far from the buses, no one else to drive; rarer with regular eye tests, a partner who drives, a town with good buses.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *At dusk on the ring road a cyclist appears at {Ns} bonnet as if out of nowhere. {N} stamps on the brake, the bike wobbles past, and the rider's shout carries through the closed window.* (any color)  
> *Every few years the licence form asks whether {Ns} eyes meet the standard, and {N} has always ticked yes.* (White)  
> *{N} replays it: the cyclist had lights. They were there all along, and {Ns} eyes simply did not catch them.* (Blue)  
> *Without the car {N} would depend on others for every errand, every visit, every scrap of independence.* (Black)  
> *{Ns} hands are shaking on the wheel, and {N} wants to roar at the cyclist, at the dark, at getting old.* (Red)  
> *The light goes earlier every autumn, and lately {Ns} eyes seem to go with it.* (Green)  

- **report the near miss and your eyesight to the licensing office yourself** (White; works 70% of the time; value: conformity, universalism; loses access to driving licence; leaves: owned up)
- **book an eye test for the next morning, and find out exactly what is wrong** (Blue; works 82% of the time; value: self-direction, security)
- **say nothing, and stop driving after dark, so nobody need ever know** (Black; works 76% of the time; value: self-direction, security; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **shout after the cyclist, then drive on home as if nothing happened** (Red; works 74% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **park the car, walk the last mile home, and leave the keys on the hook** (Green; works 74% of the time; value: security, tradition (acceptance); body: light)
- **have the cataract operation the optician has been urging for years** (White-Blue-Green (Bant); works 75% of the time; value: security)
- **tell the family that night, and let them take the car keys** (White-Red-Green (Naya); works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, security)
- **sell the car the same week, and spend the money on taxis** (White-Black-Red (Mardu); works 85% of the time; value: self-direction, security; builds self-control)
- **buy a car with every sensor and camera going, and keep on driving** (Blue-Black-Red (Grixis); works 60% of the time; value: self-direction, power)
- **map who in the street drives where, and trade favours for lifts** (Blue-Black-Green (Sultai); works 65% of the time; value: security, benevolence; binds you; leaves: made a friend)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The fright passes, and {N} finds a way of getting about that frightens nobody. / Within a month {N} has settled into a new routine, and sleeps better for it.  
If it fails: A month later {N} clips a parked van in the rain, and the questions start. / {N} sits in the kitchen turning the car keys over, and the house feels very small.

### up the ladder to clear the gutters

mature, elder, ages 55 to 100 · life event · mixed · life: home, body · with: child, neighbour, partner

Modern Earth: autumn leaves have blocked the gutters again, the ladder is in the shed, and you are not as steady as you were.

How often (per year by stage, child to elder): 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.03, 0.05; moved by: health-.3 money-.2 ties-.2.
In words: estimate: about 3 in 100 people in midlife and 5 in 100 elders a year face a job up a ladder they are no longer steady enough for; well over 100,000 people a year in the United States are treated in hospital after a fall from a ladder, and the old are the likeliest to be admitted or to die of it (D'Souza 2007, American Journal of Preventive Medicine); likelier with a house of one's own, living alone, little money for help, a lifetime of doing it oneself; rarer with a flat, family or neighbours close by, money for a firm, a bad fall already.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The gutters are full of leaves again and water is spilling down the front wall. The old ladder is in the shed, and {N} is not as steady on their feet as they were.* (any color)  
> *{child} made {N} promise, after the last fall, never to go up a ladder alone again. The water keeps dripping all the same.* (White)  
> *{N} knows the angle a ladder should stand at and how to tie it off. Knowing it and doing it at this age are two different things.* (Blue)  
> *The firm that does gutters wants a day's wages for twenty minutes' work, and {N} did this job for forty years without paying anyone.* (Black)  
> *It is a bright, cold morning, {N} feels good today, and the job would take ten minutes.* (Red)  
> *Every autumn of {Ns} life the leaves have come down and someone has gone up to clear them. That someone was always {N}.* (Green)  

- **keep your promise, and ring a firm to do it properly** (White; works 88% of the time; value: conformity, security; leaves: kept your word)
- **set the ladder at the right angle, tie it off, and go up slowly** (Blue; works 82% of the time; value: self-direction, achievement; body: heavy; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **find someone at the pub who will do it for cash, no questions asked** (Black; works 74% of the time; value: security, power)
- **nip up the ladder right now and get it done before anyone can fuss** (Red; works 72% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; body: heavy; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **go up as you have every autumn of your life, and trust your hands** (Green; works 80% of the time; value: tradition; body: heavy; builds habit; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **ask the council's handyman scheme for older people, which costs next to nothing** (White means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: security, achievement)
- **rig a pole and a hose to clear the gutter from the ground** (Blue means, Red end; works 68% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: learned a skill)
- **guilt your grown child into coming over on Sunday to do it** (Black means, Green end; works 76% of the time; value: security)
- **bang on the neighbour's door and talk them into doing it today, for lunch** (Red means, White end; works 74% of the time; value: benevolence, security)
- **watch where the water runs in the next storm, and learn what the house needs** (Green means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction; leaves: learned a skill)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The gutters run clear by lunchtime, and the dripping stops. / The job gets done, and {N} sits down with a cup of tea feeling about forty.  
If it fails: The ladder shifts on the wet path, and {N} ends up on the grass with a wrist that will not bend. / Weeks go by, the leaves stay put, and damp spreads across the front bedroom wall.

- **get the teacher to write a glowing note about you for the new school** (Black; works 80% of the time; value: achievement; told as: get the teacher to write a glowing note about them for the new school)

- **walk round the playground one last time and say goodbye to each corner of it** (Green; works 95% of the time; value: tradition)
- **ask the teacher what the big school will really be like, and listen to every word** (White means, Blue end; works 88% of the time; value: self-direction, security)
- **find out who else is going to your new school, and decide who to stick with** (Blue means, Black end; works 80% of the time; value: security, power)
- **sell your old textbooks to the year below at the gate, and spend it on summer** (Black means, Red end; works 70% of the time; value: hedonism, achievement)
- **hug your best friend, crying, and swear that nothing between the two of you will change** (Red means, Green end; works 72% of the time; value: benevolence; binds you; told as: hug their best friend, crying, and swear that nothing between the two of them will change)
- **stay behind to help take down the old displays, as the leavers always have** (Green means, White end; works 88% of the time; value: tradition, conformity)

If it fails: The bell goes before {N} has said goodbye to anyone who mattered. / Something small goes wrong in front of the whole school, and it is the thing {N} remembers.

### the first morning at the big school

juvenile, ages 11 to 13 · everyday · mixed · life: school · with: friend, parent, a form tutor, the older pupils

Modern Earth: the first morning at secondary school: a timetable you cannot read, four floors of corridors, and pupils who look like grown-ups.

In words: Nearly every child, once, on the first morning at secondary or middle school, at 10 to 12; in England nearly all pupils start secondary school at 11 (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *On the first morning at the big school {N} stands in a corridor with a timetable that makes no sense, while pupils who look like grown adults stream past on both sides.* (any color)  
> *The uniform is stiff, the tie took three tries, and the school rules are printed inside the planner. {N} has read them twice on the bus.* (White)  
> *Four floors, three staircases and a room called L14 that seems not to exist. {N} unfolds the map and starts working out the logic of the building.* (Blue)  
> *Within an hour {N} can see who runs the corridors, which table in the canteen belongs to whom, and which older pupils even the teachers handle carefully.* (Black)  
> *Nobody here holds {Ns} hand to cross anything. The bus, the gates, a thousand new faces: {N} feels the size of it like a plunge into cold water.* (Red)  
> *{friend} from the old class is in the same form, and {N} keeps {friend} in sight all morning like a landmark on a hill.* (Green)  

- **arrive early, find the form room, and sit exactly where the tutor points** (White; works 92% of the time; value: conformity, security)
- **spend the first break walking the whole building until you know every staircase** (Blue; works 88% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **make yourself useful to the older pupil who seems to run the corridor** (Black; works 70% of the time; value: power, security; told as: make themselves useful to the older pupil who seems to run the corridor)
- **get lost on purpose and look behind the doors marked staff only** (Red; works 65% of the time; value: stimulation; closed by approval: going where pupils are not allowed; backfire: caught, and a detention in the first week)
- **stay close to the one friend from your old class all day** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: security)
- **put your hand up to be form representative on the very first day** (White means, Black end; works 45% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **read the list of lunchtime clubs and sign up for the strangest one on it** (Blue means, Red end; works 85% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction)
- **gather the kids from your street into a crew that walks home together** (Black means, Green end; works 85% of the time; value: security; leaves: made a friend)
- **step in when a small kid is being shoved on the stairs** (Red means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence, universalism; body: light; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **ask the caretaker, who has been here thirty years, how the place really works** (Green means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: tradition, self-direction)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By lunchtime {N} knows where the toilets are, has a seat at a table, and has not cried once. / The day goes better than {N} feared, and on the bus home it is all {N} can talk about.  
If it fails: {N} is late to three lessons and gets the same telling-off three times. / Someone older picks {N} out on the first morning, and the day becomes something to get through.

### a friend whose family lives on the river

juvenile, ages 11 to 13 · everyday · joy · life: friends, nature, home · with: friend, parent, the friend's family

> *{friend}, a new friend from the big school, lives on a narrowboat with a family who cook on a wood stove, keep no clock and swim off the back of the boat. Every Friday {friend} asks {N} to come aboard for the weekend.* (any color)

> *The boat runs on a solar panel, a water tank and a dozen tricks that {friend}'s mother explains as she goes. {N} wants to know how every one of them works.* (Blue)  
> *{friend}'s family owns almost nothing and seems to need nothing. {N} watches them swap eggs for diesel with the next boat along, and takes note.* (Black)  
> *Leaping off the roof into the canal, fires on the towpath, whole days outdoors: {N} has never felt so free.* (Red)  
> *A heron at dawn, a kingfisher under the bridge, the water moving under the bunk all night. {N} sleeps on the boat better than anywhere.* (Green)  

- **promise to keep up at school in return for weekends aboard, and keep it** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity, security; builds self-control; leaves: kept your word)

- **let the river slow you down, and learn to sit still and watch the water** (Green; works 60% of the time; value: universalism (nature); builds habit; builds self-control; told as: let the river slow them down, and learn to sit still and watch the water)
- **bring your family down to the towpath to meet them, so both homes are one** (White means, Green end; works 55% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **promise to help your friend every week with the schoolwork the boat life misses** (Blue means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence, achievement; binds you)
- **trade your old games to the mechanic on the next boat for lessons on the engine** (Black means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: achievement, self-direction; opens new ways; gains fixing things; leaves: made a friend)

### the first Saturday in town without a grown-up

juvenile, ages 11 to 13 · everyday · joy · life: friends, freedom, money · with: friend, parent, grandparent

Modern Earth: the first Saturday you may go into town with friends on the bus, with a little money, a phone and a time to be home by.

In words: Most children, once, at about 11 to 13, the first time they may go into town with friends alone; that age has risen since the 1970s (Policy Studies Institute, children's independent mobility); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *For the first time {N} is allowed into town on the bus with {friend}, with a little money, a charged phone and a promise to be home by five.* (any color)  
> *{parent} made {N} repeat the rules at the door: stay together, keep the phone on, home by five. {N} means to keep every one of them.* (White)  
> *{N} has the bus times saved and a plan for the day: the comic shop, the market, the top floor of the library, in that order.* (Blue)  
> *Money in a pocket and nobody to say no: {N} has wanted the trainers in the sports-shop window for months, and today is the day to work out how.* (Black)  
> *The bus doors fold open on the high street, and the whole town is noise and possibility. Nobody in the world knows exactly where {N} is.* (Red)  
> *{N} walks the streets {grandparent} walked at the same age, past the same bakery and under the same clock on the town hall.* (Green)  

- **keep every rule you promised, and text home at each stop** (White; works 85% of the time; value: conformity, security; leaves: kept your word)
- **find your way round town without looking at the map, to test yourself** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction; told as: find their way round town without looking at the map, as a test)
- **spend it all on the one thing that will impress the others on Monday** (Black; works 90% of the time; value: power, hedonism; wears self-control down)
- **change the plan halfway and jump on a bus to wherever it goes** (Red; works 72% of the time; value: stimulation; closed by approval: off the agreed route; backfire: lost, with a dead phone)
- **spend the afternoon on the grass by the river, just sitting with your friends** (Green; works 92% of the time; value: hedonism, benevolence)
- **get a library card in your own name, signed and stamped** (White means, Blue end; works 92% of the time; value: self-direction, conformity; opens new ways)
- **work out which usher never checks, and get into the older film** (Blue means, Black end; works 70% of the time; value: hedonism, self-direction; closed by approval: an age-rated film; backfire: turned out, and home told)
- **talk the market trader down to half price, and spend the rest on chips** (Black means, Red end; works 70% of the time; value: hedonism, achievement)
- **buy a goldfish on impulse and carry it home on the bus in its bag** (Red means, Green end; works 88% of the time; value: hedonism, benevolence)
- **buy a small present for home with the change, as your grandparent always did** (Green means, White end; works 88% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {N} comes home on time, with a bag, a story and the feeling of being trusted. / The day goes so well that next Saturday is agreed before tea.  
If it fails: The money and the time run out together, and {parent} has to come into town to fetch {N}. / Something goes wrong in town, and it is a while before {N} is let go alone again.

### the table where you sit now

juvenile, ages 11 to 13 · everyday · mixed · life: friends, school · with: friend, grandparent, rival, the new crowd

Modern Earth: by the second term you have a table in the canteen and a crowd of your own, and your best friend from the old school sits at another one.

In words: Most children, once, in the first terms at secondary school, as friendships regroup; many primary school friendships fade after the move (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

> *By the second term {N} has a regular table in the canteen and a crowd to sit with. {friend}, the best friend from the old school, sits two tables away with other people now.* (any color)  
> *Every table has its rules about who sits where, who saves whose seat and who gets asked. {N} knows them now, and knows {friend} is no longer inside them.* (White)  
> *{N} watches the canteen like a map: who moved table this week, who is drifting, who brought {friend} into their group and why.* (Blue)  
> *{Ns} new table is one along from the window, and the window table is where the people everyone watches sit. One more step and {N} is there.* (Black)  
> *Sometimes {N} looks across at {friend} laughing with strangers and feels it like a stitch in the side.* (Red)  
> *Friends come and go like the seasons, {grandparent} says. {N} is not sure yet whether to believe it.* (Green)  

- **ask the new kid who eats alone to come and sit at your table** (White; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **keep a friend at every table, and belong to none of them completely** (Blue; works 60% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **drop the friends who are going nowhere, and move up to the window table** (Black; works 60% of the time; value: power, achievement; leaves: made an enemy)
- **march over to your old friend's table and sit down as if nothing has changed** (Red; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence, stimulation)
- **let the old friendship rest, trusting it is still there underneath** (Green; works 55% of the time; value: security, tradition)
- **tell the head about the window table's vaping, and move in when they are gone** (White means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: power, conformity; closed by approval: telling on classmates; backfire: everyone learns who told)
- **start a lunchtime club for the game you love, and see who turns up** (Blue means, Red end; works 55% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation)
- **keep your old friend close in secret, while being seen with the new crowd** (Black means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: security, benevolence)
- **tell your table to stop mocking a kid from your old school, and mean it** (Red means, White end; works 70% of the time; value: universalism, benevolence)
- **ask your grandparent how they kept their oldest friend for sixty years** (Green means, Blue end; works 80% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {N} ends the year with a place that feels like {Ns} own, and nobody who mattered left behind. / The tables settle, and {N} finds that a friendship can change shape without ending.  
If it fails: {N} picks a side, and the other side remembers. / By summer {N} has a table but nobody at it {N} could call in trouble.

### pens down on the last exam

young adult, ages 17 to 20 · everyday · joy · life: school, friends · with: friend, parent, a teacher, an uncle

Modern Earth: the invigilator says pens down on your very last school exam, and outside the hall it is summer.

- **go back in and thank the teachers who got you through, one by one** (White; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; told as: go back in and thank the teachers who got them through, one by one)

- **cram into a friend's car and race the others to the coast, music up** (Red; works 85% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **sit on the field where you sat at eleven, and let it all sink in** (Green; works 88% of the time; value: tradition)
- **organise the whole year's week of camping on the coast, as everyone promised** (White means, Red end; works 68% of the time; value: hedonism, benevolence)
- **set off on the long coast walk you mapped out during revision** (Blue means, Green end; works 85% of the time; value: universalism (nature), self-direction)
- **ask the head for a reference now, while your name is still fresh** (Black means, White end; works 85% of the time; value: achievement, security)
- **on a whim, sign up for the summer language course that starts on Monday** (Red means, Blue end; works 82% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **ring your uncle tonight and take the job in the family trade he always promised** (Green means, Black end; works 70% of the time; value: security, achievement)

If it fails: The relief does not come; {N} feels oddly empty, as if something has been taken away. / The night gets out of hand, and the morning brings a mess to sort out.

### the morning you leave home

young adult, ages 17 to 20 · everyday · mixed · life: home, family · with: parent, sibling, grandparent

Modern Earth: the car is packed to the roof, your room is stripped to the mattress, and today you leave home to live on your own.

In words: Nearly everyone, once, the first time they move out of the parental home, often at 18 to 25; the EU average age is about 26, nearer 21 in the Nordic countries (Eurostat); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The car is packed to the roof, {Ns} room is stripped to the bare mattress, and {parent} has been up since five, pretending to tidy.* (any color)  
> *{N} has a folder: the tenancy, the bank card, a list of what goes where. Leaving home is a job to be done properly.* (White)  
> *{N} looks round the bare room and tries to work out which things were truly {Ns} and which only came with the house.* (Blue)  
> *No more asking, no more curfews, no more queueing for the bathroom behind {sibling}: from tonight {N} answers to nobody.* (Black)  
> *{N} has wanted this day for years, and now that it is here {Ns} throat is tight and {N} cannot look at {parent}.* (Red)  
> *{grandparent} has come round to wave {N} off, the way the family has always seen its young ones go, and presses something folded into {Ns} hand.* (Green)  

- **say a proper goodbye, and promise to ring home every Sunday** (White; works 80% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; builds habit)
- **pack only what you used this year, and leave the rest behind for good** (Blue; works 90% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **take the good duvet, the toaster and anything else nobody will miss** (Black; works 90% of the time; value: hedonism, power)
- **go quickly, without a long goodbye, while you still can** (Red; works 90% of the time; value: self-direction; told as: go quickly, without a long goodbye, while they still can)
- **take a cutting from the garden and a jar of the family's jam** (Green; works 92% of the time; value: tradition)
- **let your parents drive you there and make up the new bed, as they want to** (White means, Green end; works 88% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **brief your younger sibling on everything they need to know about your parents** (Blue means, White end; works 88% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **sell your old things online first, to pay for a term of books** (Black means, Blue end; works 85% of the time; value: achievement)
- **tell your parents you will never need their money again** (Red means, Black end; works 50% of the time; value: self-direction, power; says who you are)
- **set off with nothing but a rucksack, the way your grandparent left their village** (Green means, Red end; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction, tradition)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {N} unpacks the first box in the new room, and the strangeness turns slowly into a beginning. / The goodbye is the right size, and {N} leaves with something settled between {N} and home.  
If it fails: The goodbye goes badly, and the first night in the new room is lonely in a way {N} did not expect. / Something that mattered is left behind, and the first week starts with a panic.

### work and a room abroad, if you go this month

Modern Earth: a cousin abroad has a job in the family restaurant and a room above it for you, if you can be on a plane before the month is out.

> *A cousin abroad has a job going in the family's restaurant and a spare room above it, if {N} can be on a plane before the month is out.* (any color)

> *The pay is better than anything at home, the rent is almost nothing, and the cousin knows people. A year there could set {N} up.* (Black)  
> *Sun, the sea, a life nobody at home can picture. {N} said yes in {Ns} heart before the message had finished.* (Red)

- **turn it down and take up the college place, as agreed** (White; works 85% of the time; value: conformity, security; leaves: turned down a chance)

- **go, work every hour there is, and send nothing home until you have a stake** (Black; works 70% of the time; value: achievement, power; builds habit; builds self-control; gains savings; leaves: moved away)
- **book the flight tonight and tell everyone afterwards** (Red; works 75% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; takes the title waiter or bartender; leaves: moved away)
- **go, and live with that branch of the family while it feels like home** (Green; works 68% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; opens new ways; gains family abroad; leaves: moved away)
- **defer the college place for a year, properly and in writing, and then go** (White means, Blue end; works 65% of the time; value: self-direction, security; leaves: moved away)
- **go, and quietly learn the cousin's recipes and suppliers for a place of your own** (Blue means, Black end; works 65% of the time; value: achievement, power; closed by approval: taking the family's trade secrets; backfire: a feud that splits the family; leaves: moved away)
- **go without a work permit, and take your chances with cash jobs** (Black means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; closed by law: working without a permit; backfire: found out, sent home and barred from returning; leaves: broke the law)
- **go, fall for the place, and decide there and then to put down roots** (Red means, Green end; works 45% of the time; value: security, self-direction; takes the title immigrant)
- **stay, because the family needs a hand at home this year** (Green means, White end; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; builds self-control; leaves: turned down a chance)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The choice holds, and within a year {N} has a life that fits it. / Doors open along the road {N} chose, and {N} turns out to be ready for them.

young adult, ages 17 to 20 · everyday · mixed · life: work, school · with: mentor, parent, grandparent, a cousin
