- **take it, and ask for your grandfather's old tools to start with** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: tradition; says who you are, binds you; takes the title apprentice)
- **keep the college place, because the qualification will pay more in the end** (White means, Black end; works 70% of the time; value: achievement, security; leaves: turned down a chance)
- **look for a trade that travels, and take a job rigging stages for touring shows** (Blue means, Red end; works 55% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; opens new ways; takes the title stage technician)

Modern Earth: your first proper payslip lands on a Friday, the rent goes out on the Monday, and what is left in between is yours to decide.

- **pay the rent and the bills first, and live on whatever is left** (White; works 85% of the time; value: security, conformity; builds habit; builds self-control)
- **log every penny for a month, then set a budget that actually works** (Blue; works 85% of the time; value: self-direction, security; builds habit; builds self-control)
- **put a slice of every payslip into investments from the first month, untouchable** (Black; works 80% of the time; value: power, achievement; builds habit; builds self-control; gains savings)
- **spend the whole first payslip in one glorious weekend** (Red; works 92% of the time; value: hedonism; builds habit; wears self-control down)
- **send a little home every month, as your parents once did for theirs** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; builds habit, binds you; builds self-control)
- **save for three months, then take the trip you promised yourself** (White means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: hedonism, self-direction; builds self-control; told as: save for three months, then take the trip they promised themselves)
- **learn to cook properly from scratch, so a little money feeds you all week** (Blue means, Green end; works 85% of the time; value: security, self-direction; leaves: learned a skill; told as: learn to cook properly from scratch, so a little money feeds them all week)
- **do the landlord's small repairs in exchange for a lower rent** (Black means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: security, power)
- **on impulse, pay a term up front for the evening class you always wanted** (Red means, Blue end; works 80% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; opens new ways; builds self-control)
- **furnish the room from skips and family attics, and bank what you save** (Green means, Black end; works 75% of the time; value: security, power; closed by law: taking from skips without asking; backfire: a row with the owner, or the police at the door)

### the birthday party that ends at eleven

adult, ages 24 to 32 · everyday · mixed · life: friends, self · with: friend, parent, partner, sibling

> *At {Ns} birthday party half the guests leave at eleven, for babysitters, early starts and long drives home. {N} stands in the kitchen with a glass and the sudden sense that something has ended.* (any color)

> *{N} counts it up, half amused: a pension statement, a dentist twice a year, opinions about gutters. When did all of that happen?* (Blue)

- **thank everyone who came with a toast, and see the last ones safely out** (White; works 92% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)

### the owner wants to retire

- **find out who would want the lease, and ask the owner for a finder's share** (Blue means, Black end; works 50% of the time; value: power)
- **take the last months' pay, and spend it on the trip you always talked about** (Black means, Red end; works 85% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; gives up the title shop assistant; leaves: turned down a chance)
- **throw the owner a farewell party in the street, and let the town say goodbye** (Red means, Green end; works 85% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; leaves: made a friend)

> *A senior carer checks the others' work, signs off the care plans and answers for it when something goes wrong. {N} has the record for it.* (White)  
> *Nursing means anatomy, drugs, exams and placements on the wards. For a year {N} has been wondering what the nurses know that {N} does not.* (Blue)  
> *Two families on the round have asked {N} to work for them directly, for more an hour than the agency pays. {N} has not said no yet.* (Black)  
> *{N} loves the clients and hates the rota, the mileage and the fifteen-minute visits. Some days {N} wants to tear the whole system up.* (Red)  
> *The retired teacher on the hill, the man with the parrot, the twins' grandmother: {N} knows every kitchen, every cat and every bad day. Leaving the round would mean leaving them.* (Green)  

- **take the senior carer's post, and the night phone with it** (White; works 70% of the time; value: conformity, benevolence; takes the title shift manager)
- **start the nursing degree part time: four years of evenings and placements** (Blue; works 45% of the time; value: achievement, self-direction; opens new ways, says who you are, binds you; gains professional registration)
- **work for the two families directly, cash in hand** (Black; works 70% of the time; value: power, achievement; closed by law: undeclared cash work, and a contract that forbids taking clients; backfire: the agency sues and the tax office writes; binds you; gains loyal clientele; leaves: broke the law)
- **tell the office the fifteen-minute visits are cruel, and refuse to rush** (Red; works 55% of the time; value: benevolence, universalism; closed by approval: refusing the rota; backfire: taken off the round; leaves: defied an authority)
- **stay on the round with the clients you know** (Green; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; leaves: turned down a chance)
- **do the medication training, which lifts the hourly rate** (White means, Black end; works 85% of the time; value: achievement, security; leaves: learned a skill)
- **look into care work abroad, where the pay is better and the winters shorter** (Blue means, Red end; works 60% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction)
- **bargain for a round close to home, to be there for your own family** (Black means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence (family), security)
- **stand up at the union meeting about the unpaid travel time** (Red means, White end; works 60% of the time; value: universalism)
- **ask the oldest carer at the agency what she would choose, in your place** (Green means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: tradition, self-direction; told as: ask the oldest carer at the agency what she would choose in their place)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {N} chooses, and the first months on the new path feel like a door opening. / {boss} shakes {Ns} hand on it, and the clients have heard the news before the week is out.  
If it fails: The new path costs more than {N} reckoned, in hours, money and sleep. / Nothing comes of it: the post goes to someone else, and the round goes on as before.

### the first client moves into a home

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 25 to 75 · everyday · trouble · life: work, care, loss · with: a client, the client's daughter, boss

Modern Earth: the woman you have visited every morning for nine years is moving into a care home, and on the last morning she asks you to help her pack.

In words: Most long-serving home care workers, once, after years on the rounds; many home care clients move into residential care in time (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *Nine years ago she was {Ns} second client; since then she has outlived her husband, two cats and four agencies. Now her legs have gone, her daughter has found a place in a care home, and on the last morning she asks {N} to help her choose what to take.* (any color)

> *Nine years of mornings: {N} knows how she takes her tea, which pills make her sick, what she says when she is frightened. None of it is in the home's forms.* (Blue)  
> *She has said more than once that {N} should have the gold watch on the dresser. The agency rules forbid gifts, and nobody else is in the room.* (Black)  
> *{N} has buried feelings about a dozen clients in nine years. This one is going to be hard, and {N} can feel it rising already.* (Red)  
> *People grow old, the legs go, the house is sold. {N} has seen it many times, and still it comes like the end of a season.* (Green)  

- **do the handover by the book, and sign off nine years of care plans** (White; works 85% of the time; value: conformity, benevolence)
- **write the home's staff a list of every small thing she likes** (Blue; works 85% of the time; value: benevolence; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **take the watch she presses on you, and say nothing to the agency** (Black; works 75% of the time; value: power, hedonism; closed by approval: gifts from clients are forbidden; backfire: the daughter asks where the watch went, and a disciplinary follows; leaves: hid a wrong; told as: take the watch she presses on them, and say nothing to the agency)
- **hand in your notice that week: nine years of goodbyes is enough** (Red; works 85% of the time; value: self-direction; gives up the title care worker)
- **help her choose the few things that matter, and let the rest go** (Green; works 78% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition (acceptance))
- **sign up for the end-of-life care course the agency runs** (White means, Blue end; works 80% of the time; value: achievement, benevolence; gains home nursing)
- **ask for the coordinator's job, off the road, now that you know every round** (Blue means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: achievement, power; takes the title shift manager)
- **slip the home's manager some chocolates, to get her the garden-view room** (Black means, Red end; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, hedonism)
- **cry with her over the boxes, and let it be what it is** (Red means, Green end; works 85% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **ask the home to let her bring the cat, and offer to visit them both** (Green means, White end; works 40% of the time; value: benevolence)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: She goes in her best coat, with the photographs and a small bag of what matters, and holds {Ns} hand at the door. / Two weeks later a card arrives at the agency in a shaky hand, with {Ns} name on it.  
If it fails: She cries all the way to the home, and {N} cannot shake it for a week. / The handover is lost in the home's paperwork, and the first news from her daughter is bad.

### week six of basic training

juvenile, young adult, adult, ages 16 to 30 · everyday · mixed · life: work, body · with: boss, colleague, parent, the other recruits

Modern Earth: halfway through basic training: the runs before dawn, the kit inspections, and a section that sinks or swims together.

In words: Every new soldier, once, at 16 to 30, halfway through basic training; it lasts about 10 weeks in the US Army and 14 in the British Army; likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *Week six of basic training: up at five, three miles before breakfast, kit laid out to the inch for inspection, and a corporal who finds something wrong every time. One recruit in {Ns} section is falling behind, and the whole section pays for it.* (any color)  
> *Everything here has a right way: the bed, the boots, the drill, the way to stand. {N} finds an odd comfort in it.* (White)  
> *{N} has worked out what the corporal checks first, and in what order. There is a system under all the shouting.* (Blue)  
> *The best recruit leads the section at the passing-out parade. {N} wants it, and watches who else does.* (Black)  
> *{Ns} feet are blistered and {Ns} lungs burn on every hill, and still, at the top, {N} feels more alive than ever before.* (Red)  
> *Six weeks ago they were twelve strangers; now they eat, sleep, run and suffer together. {N} has never been part of anything like it.* (Green)  

- **report every slip the struggling recruit makes, so the section stops paying** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity; closed by approval: informing on a comrade; backfire: the section freezes them out; leaves: made an enemy)
- **learn the drill and the kit list cold, until you can do them in the dark** (Blue; works 80% of the time; value: achievement; leaves: learned a skill)
- **push to lead the section at the parade, and make sure the corporal sees it** (Black; works 60% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **run the hills on the blisters, and finish every run near the front** (Red; works 80% of the time; value: stimulation, achievement; body: heavy; builds habit; builds self-control; gains keeping fit)
- **lean on the section like family, and let them lean on you** (Green; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence (in-group); leaves: made a friend; told as: lean on the section like family, and let them lean back)
- **carry the struggling recruit's pack up the last hill as well as your own** (White means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence; closed by approval: against the instructors' orders; backfire: both recruits punished; body: heavy; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **set up a buddy system so nobody in the section falls behind** (Blue means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, security)
- **make yourself the corporal's favourite with every extra duty going** (Black means, White end; works 75% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **volunteer for the hardest test on the course, to find out what you are made of** (Red means, Blue end; works 60% of the time; value: stimulation, achievement; body: heavy)
- **go home: sign the discharge papers while you still can** (Green means, Black end; works 85% of the time; value: security; wears self-control down; gives up the title soldier; leaves: came home)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: At the passing-out parade {N} marches in step, and somewhere in the crowd {parent} is crying. / {N} comes through week six fitter and steadier than ever, and the corporal, once, nods.  
If it fails: A shin injury puts {N} back three weeks, to start again with a new section. / The section is punished for {Ns} mistake, and the barrack room goes cold for days.

If it works: {N} signs, or does not, with a clear head, and the spring comes in on a new footing. / The choice opens doors {N} did not know were there, and the first months prove it right.

### a section of nineteen-year-olds

young adult, adult, mature, ages 24 to 55 · everyday · mixed · life: work, community · with: colleague, boss, the young soldiers, partner

Modern Earth: after many years in the army you lead a section of soldiers barely out of school, on what may be your last tour abroad.

- **use your contacts to put the brightest of them on the officers' course** (Black means, Blue end; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, achievement)
- **take the corporal aside, and make him afraid to pick on the youngest again** (Red means, Black end; works 70% of the time; value: power; closed by law: threatening a fellow soldier; backfire: a charge, and the stripe taken)
- **hand in your notice for the end of the tour, and go and live** (Green means, Red end; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction, hedonism; takes the title veteran; gives up the title soldier)

If it works: All eight of them come home at the end of the tour, and the youngest shakes {Ns} hand at the airport. / The section pulls together under {N}, and {boss} says so in the report.  
If it fails: The tour goes hard, and {N} brings home a weight that does not lift for a long time. / The choice costs {N} the stripe, the trust of the young ones, or both.

### the back row on the first Monday

young adult, adult, mature, ages 21 to 70 · everyday · mixed · life: work, school · with: colleague, boss, the pupils, mentor

Modern Earth: your first class of your own on a Monday in September: thirty fourteen-year-olds, and a back row already testing you.

In words: Every new teacher, once, in the first week of the first term; nearly 1 in 3 new teachers in England leave within five years (DfE workforce statistics); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *Monday, September, room 14: {Ns} first class of {Ns} own. Thirty fourteen-year-olds, a lesson plan typed at midnight, and a back row that has already started, very quietly, to test the new teacher.* (any color)  
> *The seating plan is printed, the rules are on the wall, and the training said the first five minutes decide the year. {N} intends to make them count.* (White)  
> *The lesson plan is timed to the minute, with three activities and a summing-up. {N} also has a hunch it will not survive the first ten minutes.* (Blue)  
> *The back row has a leader, a tall boy with a quick tongue whom the others watch before they laugh. {N} sees that the class turns on him.* (Black)  
> *{Ns} heart is going like a drum. Somewhere under the fear is the thing that made {N} want to teach in the first place: the moment a room lights up.* (Red)  
> *These are other people's children, each with a home, a story and a bad night behind them. {N} looks at thirty faces and wonders who they are.* (Green)  

- **set the seating plan and the rules in the first five minutes, and keep them** (White; works 70% of the time; value: conformity, security; builds habit; builds self-control)
- **follow the timed plan, and note what works and what does not for next time** (Blue; works 75% of the time; value: achievement, self-direction)
- **win over the boy the back row follows, and the rest will come** (Black; works 65% of the time; value: power)
- **put the plan aside and open with the most surprising thing you know** (Red; works 60% of the time; value: stimulation)
- **learn every name by Friday, and ask each of them one thing about themselves** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence; builds self-control)
- **keep the whole back row in at break, to show who is in charge** (White means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: power, conformity; closed by approval: a whole-row detention on the first day; backfire: parents complain, and the head has words)
- **turn the lesson into a puzzle they solve in teams, against the clock** (Blue means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: stimulation)
- **strike a deal with the back row: quiet now, their music at the end** (Black means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: security, hedonism)
- **raise your voice, once and hard, the first time the back row laughs** (Red means, White end; works 60% of the time; value: conformity, security)
- **ask the teacher next door, who has had them two years, what they are like** (Green means, Blue end; works 80% of the time; value: tradition, self-direction)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By the bell the back row is laughing with {N}, not at {N}, and a quiet girl at the front stays behind to ask a question. / The lesson works better than it had any right to, and {N} sits in the empty room afterwards, grinning.  
If it fails: The back row takes the lesson apart, and {N} drives home and sits in the car outside the house for twenty minutes. / The head of department walks in at the worst moment, and writes something down.

If it works: The choice turns out well, and by the summer {N} cannot imagine having chosen otherwise. / The head stops {N} in the corridor in June to say how much difference it has made.

- **let the sting pass, and come in tomorrow as on any other day** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: tradition (acceptance), security; builds self-control)
- **write the incident up so the record shows you followed procedure** (White means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: security, power; closed by approval: shading an official record; backfire: the camera footage shows otherwise)
- **find the fastest fix, then slip out before it turns into a meeting** (Blue means, Red end; works 75% of the time; value: hedonism, self-direction; wears self-control down)
- **bring cakes in next morning and let the mistake become a crew joke** (Black means, Green end; works 88% of the time; value: benevolence, security)

- **congratulate the newcomer, and wait for your season to come round** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: tradition (patience), benevolence; builds self-control)
- **ask for a fair trial for the place next season, in front of everyone** (White means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: achievement, power)
- **practise on your own every day until you are plainly better** (Blue means, Red end; works 60% of the time; value: achievement, stimulation; builds habit; builds self-control)
- **make a friend of the newcomer, and make the two of you the group's core** (Black means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: power, benevolence; leaves: made a friend)
- **stand up at the next meeting and say plainly that it was unfair** (Red means, White end; works 55% of the time; value: universalism; leaves: defied an authority)
- **ask the oldest member whether this has happened before, and how it ended** (Green means, Blue end; works 85% of the time; value: tradition)

If it works: By the next season the bitterness has gone, and {N} has a place that fits. / The leaders think again, and {N} gets a turn after all.  
If it fails: The rift with {rival} hardens, and the group starts to feel like two camps. / Nothing changes, and {N} spends the season on the edge of things.

### the newer members want to change how it is done

juvenile, young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 14 to 90 · everyday · mixed · life: community · with: elder, rival, friend

Modern Earth: you have been {title} for many years, and the newer members want to change the way the group has always done things.

- **insist that only members of long standing may vote on the change** (White; works 60% of the time; value: conformity, tradition; closed by approval: changing the rules to win; backfire: the newer members walk out; says who you are)
- **dig out the old records and show which changes were tried before** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: universalism, security)
- **lead the change yourself, so it goes the way you want** (Black; works 60% of the time; value: power; gains not to be crossed)

- **keep the one or two old customs that matter most, and let the rest go** (Green; works 65% of the time; value: tradition)
- **propose a trial season with the new ways, and an honest look at the end** (White means, Red end; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction, universalism)
- **write down the group's story before the old ways are gone** (Blue means, Green end; works 80% of the time; value: tradition)
- **quietly fill the next meeting with old hands to block it** (Black means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: power, tradition; closed by approval: rigging a meeting; backfire: the newer members find out and leave)
- **go along to one of the newcomers' own gatherings and see what they love** (Red means, Blue end; works 78% of the time; value: stimulation, universalism; opens new ways)
- **keep the newcomers off the old jobs until they have served their years** (Green means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: power, tradition; closed by approval: shutting newer members out; backfire: they complain, and the old hands are told to make room; leaves: made an enemy)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The group finds a new shape, and the best of the old one survives inside it. / Old hands and newcomers end the season at one table, arguing about something else.  
If it fails: The group splits, and half the old faces stop coming. / The change goes through over {Ns} head, and {N} feels like a guest in a group {N} helped build.

### someone has to carry it on after you

- **compare notes on how each of your families used to argue** (Blue means, Green end; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **agree a truce on terms that suit you, and get it said out loud** (Black means, White end; works 70% of the time; value: power, security; told as: agree a truce on terms that suit them, and get it said out loud)
- **storm out for the night, and come back with a clearer head** (Red means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction; wears self-control down)

If it fails: The argument goes round in circles for days and leaves a mark on both of them. / Words said that night are remembered for years.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The depot has redrawn the rounds. {Ns} gains eighty doors, a steep hill, and a handheld that logs every minute {N} stands still.* (any color)  
> *There are agreed limits on how long a round may take, signed years ago. {N} wonders whether anyone upstairs has read them lately.* (White)  
> *{N} spreads the new map on the kitchen table and starts working out a better order for the eighty extra doors.* (Blue)  
> *The new round passes the business park, where someone with a van could pick up plenty of private parcel work.* (Black)  
> *Eighty more doors and a machine on the belt timing every breath. {N} feels the old pleasure of the round drain away in a day.* (Red)  
> *{N} has walked the old streets for nine years and knows where every dog sleeps. Half of them now go to a stranger.* (Green)  

- **log the extra hours every day and take the figures to the union rep** (White; works 40% of the time; value: conformity, security)
- **redraw the walk order yourself until the round fits the shift** (Blue; works 80% of the time; value: achievement, self-direction; leaves: learned a skill)
- **take the voluntary redundancy and put it into a courier van of your own** (Black; works 55% of the time; value: achievement, self-direction; binds you; gives up the title postal worker; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **walk out of the briefing with the others when the new rounds are read** (Red; works 25% of the time; value: self-direction; closed by approval: an unofficial walkout; backfire: a written warning; leaves: defied an authority)
- **ask to keep the streets you know, even if it means the earlier shift** (Green; works 50% of the time; value: tradition, security)
- **write down which old customers need care, for whoever takes your streets** (White means, Green end; works 95% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **time the new rounds with a stopwatch and show they break the agreement** (Blue means, White end; works 45% of the time; value: universalism (fairness))
- **buy the depot manager a pint and find out what the next shake-up holds** (Black means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: power)
- **attack the new round flat out, and claim every minute of overtime it takes** (Red means, Black end; works 68% of the time; value: achievement, power)
- **take the new hill as a gift: the best view on the round, every morning** (Green means, Red end; works 88% of the time; value: stimulation, hedonism)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: Within a month the new round has a rhythm, and {N} is home by two most days. / The depot gives way on part of it, and the worst of the hill goes to a van round.  
If it fails: The new round runs late every day, and the handheld marks {N} as the slowest on the shift. / A letter about performance turns up in {Ns} pigeonhole, and {colleague} gets the same one.

### a message from home on the night watch

young adult, adult, mature, ages 16 to 65 · everyday · trouble · life: work, family · with: parent, sibling, boss

Modern Earth: a message from home reaches you on watch at sea: you can reply, but you cannot be there.

In words: Most merchant seafarers, a few times in a career, being away for months at a time; there are about 1.9 million seafarers (BIMCO and ICS 2021); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *A message from home arrives during {Ns} night watch: {parent} is in hospital after a fall. {N} can reply, but cannot be there.* (any color)  
> *The watch is {Ns} to keep until four, and the bridge cannot be left. {N} reads the message twice and keeps an eye on the radar.* (White)  
> *{N} works it out: eleven days to the next port, a flight from there, two days more to get home. The arithmetic does not help.* (Blue)  
> *The contract runs four more months, and breaking it costs the bonus and perhaps the next berth. {N} has worked too hard for this one.* (Black)  
> *{N} wants to be at the bedside now, and instead there are four hours of dark water and a blinking screen.* (Red)  
> *The ship moves on through the night, and far behind it {parent} lies in a hospital bed. Sea and home have always pulled at {N} like two tides.* (Green)  

- **finish the watch properly, then write a long reply at the end of it** (White; works 88% of the time; value: conformity, benevolence; builds self-control)
- **find out from the hospital exactly how serious it is before deciding anything** (Blue; works 60% of the time; value: security)
- **decide the contract comes first: the money keeps the whole family going** (Black; works 88% of the time; value: security, achievement; builds self-control)
- **record a voice message on the bridge wing, saying everything you feel** (Red; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **write back calmly that you will be home when the voyage ends** (Green; works 83% of the time; value: tradition; builds self-control)
- **ask the captain for a satellite call, as the rules allow in a family emergency** (White means, Blue end; works 78% of the time; value: security)
- **work out the cheapest way home that still keeps your contract bonus** (Blue means, Black end; works 45% of the time; value: achievement, security)
- **offer the captain extra watches in return for signing off at the next port** (Black means, Red end; works 45% of the time; value: benevolence, self-direction)
- **ring home and sing down the line the song your parent always sang** (Red means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **ask your brother or sister to be there in your place, and keep your post** (Green means, White end; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The reply reaches home before morning, and {parent} has it read aloud on the ward. / The news from the hospital is better by the end of the watch, and {N} sleeps for once.  
If it fails: The signal drops, and the message sits unsent until the ship clears the weather. / {sibling} writes back, short and hurt: everyone else is there.

### an offer of work ashore

young adult, adult, mature, ages 16 to 65 · everyday · mixed · life: work, family · with: partner, boss, colleague

Modern Earth: after years at sea the company offers you a desk in the port office: home every night, a third less pay.

In words: Many long-serving seafarers, once or twice in a career; port office jobs are the usual step off the ships (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The company offers {N} a job ashore in the port office: home every night, a third less money, and no more horizon.* (any color)  
> *{N} has a crew who count on {N} at sea and a family who count on {N} at home, and only one of them can have {N} every day.* (White)  
> *{N} lays out the two lives on paper: the pay, the pension, the months away, the hours in traffic. The columns come out almost even.* (Blue)  
> *Ashore, {N} would be the one assigning crews instead of waiting to be assigned. The desk could lead somewhere.* (Black)  
> *{N} has never once been bored at sea. An office with a window onto the docks sounds like a cage with a view.* (Red)  
> *{partner} has planted a garden that {N} has seen in only two of the last six springs.* (Green)  

- **ask the crew and the family what they need, and go with the greater need** (White; works 60% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- **ask for six months ashore on trial before giving up the sea for good** (Blue; works 35% of the time; value: security, self-direction; opens new ways)
- **take the desk and aim to run the crewing office within two years** (Black; works 40% of the time; value: achievement, power; takes the title office clerk; gives up the title merchant seafarer)
- **turn it down without a second thought; the sea is where you belong** (Red; works 92% of the time; value: stimulation, self-direction; says who you are)
- **take the shore job and be there for every season at home at last** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; gives up the title merchant seafarer; leaves: came home)
- **stay at sea and sign up for the officer's course that raises your pay** (White means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: achievement; opens new ways, binds you; gains rank)
- **sign with a company that runs shorter rotations, two months on and two off** (Blue means, Red end; works 55% of the time; value: self-direction; binds you)
- **use the offer to bargain for shorter voyages and more leave at home** (Black means, Green end; works 50% of the time; value: benevolence, power)
- **tell the captain straight out that you stay as long as the crew does** (Red means, White end; works 78% of the time; value: benevolence; binds you)
- **wait one more voyage, and see how it feels to come home this time** (Green means, Blue end; works 85% of the time; value: self-direction)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The choice settles, and {N} sleeps well the first night after making it. / {partner} hears the news and laughs out loud down the phone.  
If it fails: The decision is made, and for months {N} keeps glancing towards the water. / The company takes the offer back while {N} is still making up {Ns} mind.

### the colonies and the calendar disagree

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 20 to 85 · everyday · mixed · life: work, nature · with: a farmer, mentor

Modern Earth: the contract says the hives go to the orchard on Monday, but after a cold spring the colonies look far from ready.

In words: Most beekeepers who rent hives for pollination, in late springs every year or two; contracts fix the dates months ahead (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The calendar says the hives go to the orchard on Monday. The colonies, slow and thin at the entrances after a cold spring, suggest otherwise.* (any color)  
> *{N} signed a contract with the orchard: forty hives on site by the first blossom. In this trade a beekeeper's word is the business.* (White)  
> *{N} has kept records for nine springs: brood frames, temperatures, flights at the entrance. This year's numbers sit lower than any before.* (Blue)  
> *The orchard pays well, and two other beekeepers would gladly take the contract next year if {N} lets the farmer down.* (Black)  
> *{N} has been itching for the blossom all winter. Waiting another week feels like holding a breath.* (Red)  
> *Bees keep their own calendar, and this spring it runs late. {N} watches the cold entrances and feels the season turning slowly.* (Green)  

- **move them on Monday as contracted, and say nothing about how weak they are** (White; works 55% of the time; value: conformity, security; closed by approval: hiding weak colonies from a client; backfire: the farmer lifts a lid; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **open every hive, count the brood frames and decide hive by hive** (Blue; works 85% of the time; value: achievement)
- **ring the farmer, explain, and agree a later date before a rival hears** (Black; works 78% of the time; value: security, power)
- **load the strongest twenty hives tonight and drive them out** (Red; works 85% of the time; value: achievement; body: heavy)
- **wait the week the bees ask for, whatever the contract says** (Green; works 50% of the time; value: universalism (nature); closed by approval: breaking the delivery date; backfire: the farmer holds back the payment; leaves: broke your word)
- **draw up a loading rota so the move can happen the hour they are ready** (White means, Red end; works 80% of the time; value: achievement)
- **feed the weak colonies syrup and pollen, and watch how they answer** (Blue means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: universalism (nature))
- **buy twenty strong hives from a neighbour to keep your word to the orchard** (Black means, White end; works 80% of the time; value: security, achievement; leaves: kept your word)
- **drive out to the orchard at dawn and look at the buds yourself** (Red means, Blue end; works 95% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **ask the old beekeeper down the valley for strong colonies on credit** (Green means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: security, achievement; binds you)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The orchard blossoms with the hives humming in it, and the farmer books forty more for next spring. / The colonies build up within the week, and the move goes smoothly at dusk.  
If it fails: Half the hives arrive weak, and the blossom passes with the bees barely flying. / The farmer rings a rival on Tuesday, and next year's contract goes with that call.

### a third of the hives dead after winter

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 20 to 85 · everyday · trouble · life: work, nature · with: mentor, partner

Modern Earth: on the first warm day of spring you open the hives and find a third of the colonies dead.

In words: Most beekeepers, every few years; US winter losses have often run 20 to 40 in 100 colonies (Bee Informed Partnership surveys); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *On the first warm day of the year {N} opens the hives and finds a third of the colonies dead, clustered on empty comb.* (any color)  
> *Losses this size are to be reported to the bee inspector, and the register has a form for it. {N} reaches for the folder.* (White)  
> *{N} sends samples off and pulls the winter's records: mites, stores, the cold snap in February. One of them did this.* (Blue)  
> *A third of the stock is gone, and a third of this year's honey money with it. {N} starts adding up what it takes to rebuild.* (Black)  
> *{N} sits on an upturned crate among the silent hives and lets the grief come out loud.* (Red)  
> *Every beekeeper loses colonies; the old ones speak of it like weather. {N} breathes in the smell of old comb and spring grass.* (Green)  

- **report the losses to the bee inspector and follow the advice to the letter** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity, security)
- **send samples to the lab, and find out what killed them before restocking** (Blue; works 78% of the time; value: achievement, security; leaves: learned a skill)
- **split the strong colonies hard and rebuild the numbers by midsummer** (Black; works 70% of the time; value: achievement)
- **drive to the queen breeder that morning and buy back everything you lost** (Red; works 85% of the time; value: self-direction; wears self-control down)
- **sell most of the hives and go back to keeping a few for love** (Green; works 72% of the time; value: security, hedonism; wears self-control down; gives up the title professional beekeeper)
- **warn the other beekeepers in the valley, so their bees are spared** (White means, Green end; works 92% of the time; value: universalism, benevolence; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **write up what you found for the beekeepers' association newsletter** (Blue means, White end; works 90% of the time; value: universalism; says who you are)
- **pay a bee scientist for a day to go through the whole apiary** (Black means, Blue end; works 90% of the time; value: achievement)
- **borrow against the house for new stock: double the hives or lose the lot** (Red means, Black end; works 35% of the time; value: achievement, power; binds you; leaves: took a wild risk)
- **let the survivors build up in their own time, and enjoy the slower year** (Green means, Red end; works 70% of the time; value: hedonism, universalism (nature))
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By midsummer the apiary is humming again, smaller but healthy. / The cause turns out to be clear and fixable, and next winter the hives come through.  
If it fails: The rebuilt colonies dwindle again by autumn, and the honey money barely covers the sugar. / The bank statement in June shows how deep the hole really is.

### one song for a divided family

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 20 to 75 · everyday · mixed · life: work, faith · with: a grieving family, colleague

Modern Earth: a family arranging a funeral cannot agree on a single religious tradition, but everyone remembers the same song.

In words: Most funeral directors, many times a year; mixed-faith and no-faith families are now common at funerals (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The family in the arrangement room cannot agree on a single religious tradition for the funeral, but every one of them remembers the same song.* (any color)  
> *There are proper forms for every faith, and {N} knows them all. The difficulty is that this family wants three of them at once.* (White)  
> *{N} listens and maps it out: the widow's church, the son's mosque, the daughter's nothing-at-all, and one old song running through all of them.* (Blue)  
> *Families choose the firm that gives them a service they can all bear, and {N} wants this to be the family that recommends the firm to the whole town.* (Black)  
> *When the song comes up the whole family starts humming it at once, then crying, and {N} feels a lump in {Ns} own throat.* (Red)  
> *Families break and mend around a death; {N} has seen it a hundred times. The song is the root they still share.* (Green)  

- **lay out each tradition's rites and help them settle on an order all accept** (White; works 55% of the time; value: conformity, tradition)
- **design a service in parts: a reading from each faith, joined by the song** (Blue; works 78% of the time; value: universalism, self-direction)
- **steer them firmly to the one plan that keeps the peace, and book it today** (Black; works 82% of the time; value: power, achievement)
- **suggest they all sing the song together at the end, unaccompanied** (Red; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **let the eldest decide for everyone, as families always used to** (Green; works 35% of the time; value: tradition; closed by approval: overruling the grieving children; backfire: a row at the graveside)
- **explain what the law requires and what is only custom, so they know their choices** (White means, Blue end; works 85% of the time; value: self-direction, universalism)
- **find out which relative is paying, and shape the plan around them** (Blue means, Black end; works 85% of the time; value: power)
- **call in a favour to get a live musician who knows the song, at short notice** (Black means, Red end; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, hedonism)
- **tell the family plainly that they are all mourning the same person** (Red means, Green end; works 72% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **let them talk it out over tea, however long it takes, then draw up the order** (Green means, White end; works 70% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The service holds all of them, and when the song begins the whole room sings. / The family leaves the arrangement room with one plan and, for once, one voice.  
If it fails: The son walks out of the meeting, and the plan has to be redrawn twice. / On the day, half the family sits on one side of the room and will not look at the other half.

### the night phone rings again

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 20 to 75 · everyday · trouble · life: work, home · with: partner, colleague, boss

Modern Earth: you are on call, and at three in the morning the phone rings for the third night running: a death at home, a family waiting.

In words: Most funeral directors on call, in a run of hard nights most winters; deaths peak in winter (ONS); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *At three in the morning the on-call phone rings for the third night running: a death at home, and a family waiting for someone to come.* (any color)  
> *Someone has to go, gently and properly, at any hour. That is the promise the firm makes, and {N} has made it too.* (White)  
> *{N} counts the hours slept this week, eleven, and knows exactly what tiredness does to judgement at a bedside.* (Blue)  
> *{colleague} has swapped out of every night this month. {N} has noticed, and has had enough of being the one who never says no.* (Black)  
> *{N} sits up with a thudding heart and, for a moment, wants to hurl the phone at the wall.* (Red)  
> *{partner} turns over in the dark and says nothing. Death keeps its own hours, and has never once asked {N} for permission.* (Green)  

- **get dressed, go, and do it as carefully as the very first time** (White; works 92% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity; says who you are)
- **log every call-out for a month and show the manager what the hours cost** (Blue; works 55% of the time; value: security; builds habit)
- **tell the colleague who dodges nights, to their face, that this one is theirs** (Black; works 65% of the time; value: power, self-direction; leaves: made an enemy)
- **go, then tell the manager at breakfast that you are taking next week off** (Red; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **go, and afterwards sit in the garden at dawn until the night has passed** (Green; works 90% of the time; value: none clear (letting it pass); builds habit)
- **report the colleague who dodges nights to the manager, by name** (White means, Black end; works 55% of the time; value: power, conformity; closed by approval: informing on a colleague; backfire: the team turns cold)
- **learn a breathing routine from a grief counsellor and use it in the car** (Blue means, Red end; works 77% of the time; value: self-direction; builds habit; builds self-control; leaves: learned a skill)
- **refuse weekend calls this month, whoever complains, and stay home** (Black means, Green end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **ring the backup colleague now, and offer to go out to the family together** (Red means, White end; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- **sit longer with the family than the job needs, and learn from their grief** (Green means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence; opens new ways; leaves: helped someone in need)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The night passes, and by the weekend the rota has room in it again. / {N} comes home at dawn, sleeps until noon, and wakes up steady.  
If it fails: The tiredness shows: a name spelt wrong on an order of service, and a family that notices. / {partner} says, quietly, that {N} is never really home any more.

### a sketch that matters more than it looks

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 18 to 75 · everyday · mixed · life: work, art · with: a client, colleague

Modern Earth: a client brings a sketch that is awkwardly drawn and deeply important, and wants it tattooed.

In words: Most tattoo artists, a few times a year; memorial pieces are among the most common requests (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *A client lays a sketch on {Ns} counter, drawn on a napkin by the client's late father: awkward, wobbly and deeply important. {N} has to improve the design without replacing its meaning.* (any color)  
> *{N} has a rule: never put lines on skin that will blur in ten years. This sketch breaks most of the rules of what holds up.* (White)  
> *{N} studies the wobbly lines. The hand was unsure, but the proportions say something, and there is a way to keep both.* (Blue)  
> *A piece like this gets photographed and shared. Done well it could bring in a dozen clients; done badly it still carries {Ns} name.* (Black)  
> *The client's eyes fill as they talk about it, and {N} feels the need to get it exactly right burning in {Ns} own hands.* (Red)  
> *Shaky lines from a hand that is gone now. {N} thinks some marks should keep the tremor of the person who made them.* (Green)  

- **explain honestly which lines will blur, and agree each change before inking** (White; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence, conformity)
- **trace it, keep every quirk, and redraw only what the needle cannot hold** (Blue; works 78% of the time; value: achievement)
- **redraw it in your own style; your name goes on the work** (Black; works 45% of the time; value: power, achievement; says who you are)
- **draw it straight onto the skin with a marker, together, until it feels right** (Red; works 78% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation)
- **tattoo it exactly as drawn, wobbles and all** (Green; works 70% of the time; value: tradition, benevolence; says who you are)
- **book a second session just to try the stencil on and live with it a week** (White means, Red end; works 80% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **ask to see more of the father's drawings, and learn his hand** (Blue means, Green end; works 75% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **refuse to ink it as it is; your studio does not put out work that blurs** (Black means, White end; works 65% of the time; value: power, conformity)
- **stay after closing and draw twenty versions until one is right** (Red means, Blue end; works 78% of the time; value: achievement; builds habit; builds self-control)
- **do it with care, then ask if you can share it, with the story, online** (Green means, Black end; works 72% of the time; value: achievement)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The client looks in the mirror for a long time, then hugs {N} without a word. / The piece heals clean, and every wobble that mattered is still there.  
If it fails: The client says it is lovely, in the voice people use when it is not. / The lines spread a little in healing, and {N} sees every fault each time the client waves.

### an ache in the tattooing wrist

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 18 to 75 · everyday · trouble · life: work, health · with: colleague, mentor

Modern Earth: after years of long sessions your wrist aches for hours after work, and the diary is full for months.

In words: Most working tattoo artists, in flares every few years after their first decade; aches and pain are common in the trade (Keester and Sommerich 2017); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *After eight-hour sessions {Ns} wrist aches long into the night, and the booking diary is full until spring.* (any color)  
> *Every client in that diary was given a date, and a deposit was taken. {N} does not like to break a booking.* (White)  
> *{N} notices the ache is worst after shading, and starts thinking about grips, angles and the weight of the machine.* (Blue)  
> *The diary is full because {N} is the best in town right now. Every cancelled session is money, and a client who might go elsewhere.* (Black)  
> *{N} loves the buzz of the machine more than anything, and the thought of putting it down even for a month is unbearable.* (Red)  
> *The body has been giving its signal for months. {N} has heard old artists talk about hands that simply stopped one day.* (Green)  

- **see a doctor, and follow whatever rest they prescribe** (White; works 70% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **switch to a lighter machine and a new grip, and track the ache for a month** (Blue; works 72% of the time; value: achievement; leaves: learned a skill)
- **hire a junior for the simple pieces, and keep the big work for yourself** (Black; works 85% of the time; value: achievement, power)
- **cancel a month of bookings at once and go travelling until the hand heals** (Red; works 82% of the time; value: stimulation, hedonism; opens new ways)
- **cut down to four days a week, and let the hand set the pace** (Green; works 75% of the time; value: security; builds self-control)
- **set yourself a firm rule: no session over four hours, ever** (White means, Green end; works 65% of the time; value: security; builds habit)
- **write a safe-working guide for the studio, so the juniors are spared it** (Blue means, White end; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence)
- **pay for sessions with a hand physiotherapist who treats musicians** (Black means, Blue end; works 85% of the time; value: achievement, security)
- **teach a weekend workshop, and earn from your name instead of your wrist** (Red means, Black end; works 70% of the time; value: achievement)
- **take the slower weeks as a gift, and draw just for the pleasure of it** (Green means, Red end; works 90% of the time; value: hedonism)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: By spring the ache has faded to a whisper, and the diary is still full. / The new routine holds, and {N} finishes a long back piece without a twinge.  
If it fails: The ache turns to numbness, and two sessions have to be cancelled in one week. / Clients drift to the studio across the road while {N} rests.

### the ending the publisher wants

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 20 to 95 · everyday · mixed · life: work, art · with: an editor, partner, friend

Modern Earth: a publisher likes your book but asks for an ending you no longer believe.

In words: Many published novelists, once or twice in a career; an editor asking for a different ending is an old story in publishing (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The publisher likes the book and wants it. They ask only for a different ending, one {N} no longer believes.* (any color)  
> *Keeping faith with the people who back a book matters to {N}. So does keeping faith with the book.* (White)  
> *{N} reads the editor's notes three times. They are not foolish notes; they point at something the last chapter has not earned.* (Blue)  
> *A contract with a real publisher, an advance, a launch: all of it rests on one chapter {N} could rewrite in a week.* (Black)

- **write the ending the publisher asks for, as well as you honestly can** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity, achievement; wears self-control down; leaves: gave in to pressure)

### defending a speaker you cannot stand

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 18 to 85 · everyday · trouble · life: cause, community · with: colleague, the street preacher, the campaign's lawyer

Modern Earth: the campaign is asked to defend a street preacher banned from the market square, whose views you find hateful.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *A street preacher whose views {N} finds hateful has been banned from the market square under a vague new bylaw, and the campaign's lawyer wants {N} to speak for his right at the hearing.* (any color)  
> *The bylaw lets an officer ban anyone whose speech "causes annoyance". Today it is the preacher; the rule does not care who comes next.* (White)  
> *{N} reads the bylaw, then the preacher's leaflets, then the bylaw again. The legal question and the personal one are not the same question.* (Blue)  
> *The hearing will be in the papers, and whoever argues it well becomes the name people call next time.* (Black)  
> *{N} has heard what he shouts in the square, and standing beside him turns {Ns} stomach. A ban on speech makes {N} angrier still.* (Red)  
> *The market square has heard preachers, hawkers and drunks for six hundred years, and the town has always found a way to live with its loudmouths.* (Green)  

- **speak for his right at the hearing, and say plainly that you reject his views** (White; works 70% of the time; value: universalism; says who you are)
- **write a careful brief on why the bylaw is too vague to stand** (Blue; works 70% of the time; value: universalism, achievement)
- **take the case on for the attention it will bring the campaign** (Black; works 85% of the time; value: power)
- **refuse to stand beside him, and say why at the campaign meeting** (Red; works 92% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **let others argue this one, and keep your strength for causes closer to home** (Green; works 90% of the time; value: security)
- **hold the campaign to its rule: every case judged on the law, not the person** (White means, Blue end; works 90% of the time; value: universalism)
- **pass a journalist the council emails you were copied into by mistake** (Blue means, Black end; works 45% of the time; value: power; closed by law: using documents sent in error; backfire: a complaint, and the campaign's name in the story; leaves: made an enemy)
- **take the case only if you never have to share a platform with him** (Black means, Red end; works 75% of the time; value: self-direction)
- **go to the square and talk with him face to face, one person to another** (Red means, Green end; works 55% of the time; value: benevolence, universalism; opens new ways)
- **propose the town's old answer: a set corner and a set hour for street speakers** (Green means, White end; works 20% of the time; value: tradition, security)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The bylaw is suspended, and nobody mistakes {Ns} defence of the right for agreement with the man. / {N} comes out of the week able to look everyone in the eye, and the campaign holds together.  
If it fails: A photo of {N} beside the preacher goes round the town, and old friends stop calling. / The hearing upholds the ban, and the campaign argues about the case for months.

- **take the seat, and shape the cameras from the inside** (Black; works 60% of the time; value: power; leaves: broke your word)

- **trade the seat for cameras kept out of the park and the side streets** (Black means, Green end; works 35% of the time; value: security)
- **lead a sit-in at the council chamber until the offer is withdrawn** (Red means, White end; works 20% of the time; value: universalism; closed by law: occupying a council building; backfire: removed by the police and charged; body: light)
- **wait and watch how the cameras work in the next town before choosing a side** (Green means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: security, self-direction; opens new ways)
- *(do nothing)*

If it fails: The cameras go up anyway, and the campaign splits over who sold out whom. / The council quietly drops the offer, and the court case drags on with no money left.

- **invite the other women from the picket line to tell it together** (Green means, White end; works 20% of the time; value: universalism, benevolence)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The programme goes out on Thursday, and the phone line fills with people who remember. / The neighbour hears the programme, cries a little, and says it was told right.  
If it fails: The recording is muddy and halting, and the station manager shelves it. / The neighbour gets cold feet and asks {N} to drop it.

### a guest who does not turn up

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 18 to 90 · everyday · trouble · life: work, community · with: a station manager, colleague, a listener

Modern Earth: the guest for your live show does not arrive, and there are forty minutes to fill.

In words: Most live radio presenters, a few times a year; volunteer guests often cancel late (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *Two minutes to the top of the hour, the guest's phone goes to voicemail, and forty minutes of live radio stretch ahead of {N} with nothing in them.* (any color)  
> *Listeners expect the programme they were promised. {N} owes them an honest word about the change, and a decent hour anyway.* (White)  
> *{N} runs through what is in the studio: a stack of records, last week's listener letters, a notebook full of half-ideas.* (Blue)  
> *Dead air is a presenter's worst enemy, and {N} will not be beaten by it. Every minute filled well proves who belongs in this chair.* (Black)  
> *{Ns} heart is pounding, and something in {N} is delighted: no script, no safety net, just a microphone and a town listening.* (Red)  
> *The station has run for thirty years on volunteers and goodwill. Shows have survived worse than an empty chair.* (Green)  

- **tell listeners honestly what happened, and play the music you promised** (White; works 92% of the time; value: conformity)
- **open the phone lines and put one good question to the town** (Blue; works 50% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation)
- **ring a local councillor you know and get them on air in ten minutes** (Black; works 65% of the time; value: achievement, power)
- **play the records you love, and tell the story behind each one** (Red; works 92% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation)
- **read out old listener letters, and let the show be gentle for once** (Green; works 85% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition)
- **follow the station's dead-air plan to the letter, and keep your slot safe** (White means, Black end; works 65% of the time; value: security, conformity)
- **turn the hour into a live quiz about the town, with a cake as the prize** (Blue means, Red end; works 68% of the time; value: stimulation, hedonism)
- **pull in whoever is in the building, the cleaner and the cook, and interview them** (Black means, Green end; works 85% of the time; value: benevolence, achievement)
- **grab the portable kit and report live from the council meeting down the road** (Red means, White end; works 40% of the time; value: universalism, stimulation)
- **ask the oldest volunteer in the building to tell how the station began** (Green means, Blue end; works 82% of the time; value: tradition, self-direction)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The hour flies by, and the station manager rings to say it was the best show of the month. / Listeners phone in all hour, and nobody misses the guest.  
If it fails: There are long silences, and {N} can hear the studio clock ticking on air. / The hour stumbles along, and the station gets two complaints by Monday.

### a roof three households cannot pay for

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 20 to 100 · everyday · trouble · life: home, money, community · with: a neighbour, a surveyor, the treasurer

Modern Earth: the cooperative's roof needs money now, and three households cannot afford their share.

In words: Most long-time co-op members, once or twice; big repairs like a roof come every few decades (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

In the story (modern Earth):

> *The surveyor's report lies on the table at the general meeting: the roof must be done before winter, and the share comes to more than a month's rent per flat. Three households say quietly that they cannot pay it.* (any color)  
> *Every member signed the same rules: shared costs, a shared say, nobody left out. {N} wants a fair answer, written down, that the rules can carry.* (White)  
> *{N} reads the report twice and starts on the numbers: the reserve fund, a loan, a cheaper repair, a longer payment plan.* (Blue)  
> *{N} can pay, and has no wish to carry three other households for years. But a leaking roof drips on everyone, and there is room to shape the deal.* (Black)  
> *{N} looks at the three faces, embarrassed in front of the whole room, and wants to stand up and say the rest will cover it, tonight.* (Red)  
> *The building has stood for ninety years, and these families have shared it for twenty. {N} feels this is the kind of trouble a home gets through together.* (Green)  

- **propose that every household pays by its income, written into the rules** (White; works 35% of the time; value: universalism)
- **work out a ten-year plan from the reserve fund and a small loan** (Blue; works 72% of the time; value: security, achievement; binds you; builds self-control)
- **pay your own share at once, and press the others to find theirs** (Black; works 72% of the time; value: security, power)
- **offer, there and then, to cover one household's share yourself** (Red; works 80% of the time; value: benevolence; binds you; leaves: helped someone in need)
- **call a work weekend, so members strip the old tiles themselves** (Green; works 45% of the time; value: benevolence, security; body: heavy)
- **vote with the majority tonight, so it is settled and nobody stews** (White means, Red end; works 78% of the time; value: conformity; wears self-control down; leaves: gave in to pressure)
- **get three more quotes, and find a repair that keeps the old slates** (Blue means, Green end; works 70% of the time; value: security, tradition)
- **offer to lend the three households the money yourself, at a little interest** (Black means, White end; works 80% of the time; value: power, security)
- **climb up with a neighbour and see the damage for yourself** (Red means, Blue end; works 95% of the time; value: self-direction; body: light)
- **let the three households pay later, in work on the building** (Green means, Black end; works 72% of the time; value: security, benevolence; binds you)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The roof is done by November, and nobody has had to leave. / The meeting finds a plan everyone can live with, and the minutes are signed with relief.  
If it fails: The argument runs on for three meetings, and the rain comes in before the scaffolding does. / One of the three households gives notice, and the stairwell is quieter for it.

### an empty flat in the cooperative

young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 20 to 100 · everyday · mixed · life: home, community · with: friend, a neighbour, the committee

Modern Earth: a flat falls empty, and the cooperative must choose who moves in, while a friend of yours needs a home.

> *The ground-floor flat is empty for the first time in eleven years. There are forty names on the waiting list, and {friend} has just asked {N}, quietly, whether there is any way up it.* (any color)

- **tell your friend plainly that the list is the list** (White; works 75% of the time; value: conformity, universalism)
- **go through the list with the committee and score each household openly** (Blue; works 78% of the time; value: universalism; says who you are)

- **welcome whoever the list brings with a house-warming from every member** (White means, Green end; works 90% of the time; value: benevolence, tradition; leaves: made a friend)
- **draft a clearer, fairer points system for every flat to come** (Blue means, White end; works 45% of the time; value: universalism)
- **push for the household with building skills, to save on repairs** (Black means, Blue end; works 75% of the time; value: achievement, security)
- **lose patience with the committee, and get them to decide that night** (Red means, Black end; works 60% of the time; value: power)
- **help your friend find another place nearby, and carry the boxes yourself** (Green means, Red end; works 65% of the time; value: benevolence; body: heavy; leaves: helped someone in need)
