- **help the town turn the old mill into a museum of the trade** (White means, Green end; works 52% of the time; value: tradition, universalism)
- **draw up a retraining scheme for everyone laid off, and take it to the council** (Blue means, White end; works 58% of the time; value: benevolence, universalism)
- **sell your long knowledge of the trade to its rivals, as a consultant** (Black means, Blue end; works 72% of the time; value: achievement, power)
- **grab the redundancy money and open a bar the very next week** (Red means, Black end; works 48% of the time; value: achievement, stimulation)
- **take the payout and the dog, and go to live by the sea** (Green means, Red end; works 80% of the time; value: hedonism, self-direction; leaves: moved away)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: {N} finds a new footing, and the loss turns slowly into a beginning. / The town pulls together, and something new grows where the mill stood.  
If it fails: Months pass with no work, and the quiet in the house grows heavy. / {N} clings to the old place long after there is nothing left to hold.

### waking up in hospital

juvenile, young adult, adult, mature, elder, ages 12 to 110 · echo · trouble · life: body, health · with: friend, parent, partner, a nurse, a doctor, the police

Modern Earth: you wake up in a hospital bed with a drip in your arm, and slowly the night comes back to you.

In words: Follows some failed risks: perhaps 1 in 4 nights that go badly wrong (an overdose, a crash, a fall) end in a hospital bed (estimate); likelier with ; rarer with .

Comes up only after: mark 'used drugs' or 'took a wild risk' on an act that failed (an overdose, a crash, a fall, a night that went wrong), 0 to 1 years later. Likelier with a heavy act (body: heavy) or one with death_if_fails; a failure far from help; rarer with friends who stayed sober and called for help early; a light act.

In the story (modern Earth):

> *{N} wakes under strip lights with a drip in one arm and a plastic band on the wrist. Slowly, in pieces, it comes back: what happened, and how it went wrong.* (any color)  
> *A nurse is going through a form at the end of the bed, asking the questions in order. {N} knows there are rules for what happens next, and honest answers are part of them.* (White)  
> *{N} reads the chart clipped to the bed before anyone comes, trying to work out what happened and how bad it was.* (Blue)  
> *{N} is already working out the story: what to say, to whom, and what nobody needs to know.* (Black)  
> *{Ns} whole body aches, and the first feeling, before fear or shame, is a fierce, odd gladness to be alive.* (Red)  
> *{friend} is asleep in the chair beside the bed, still in a coat, and must have been there all night.* (Green)  

- **tell the whole truth to anyone who asks, other people's names included** (White; works 80% of the time; value: conformity, universalism; closed by approval: naming the others; backfire: frozen out by the people named; leaves: owned up)
- **read your own notes on the desk while nobody is looking** (Blue; works 78% of the time; value: self-direction; closed by approval: reading files not meant for patients; backfire: a nurse catches it, and the doctors turn guarded)
- **get the story straight before anyone else talks, and tell it first** (Black; works 72% of the time; value: security, power)
- **pull out the drip and discharge yourself the moment you can stand** (Red; works 68% of the time; value: self-direction, stimulation; body: heavy)
- **let the family close ranks round the bed, and answer nobody's questions** (Green; works 76% of the time; value: security, tradition; closed by approval: shutting out the people who need answers; backfire: the questions come back harder; leaves: hid a wrong)
- **sign up for the course the hospital offers people who come in this way** (White means, Blue end; works 70% of the time; value: self-direction; builds habit, opens new ways)
- **find out what anyone actually knows before saying a word** (Blue means, Black end; works 72% of the time; value: security, power)
- **laugh it off with everyone, and start planning the next time** (Black means, Red end; works 78% of the time; value: hedonism, stimulation; wears self-control down)
- **cry when the family walks in, and let them see how scared you were** (Red means, Green end; works 82% of the time; value: benevolence, security)
- **make a quiet vow at the bedside to change how you live** (Green means, White end; works 74% of the time; value: tradition, conformity; binds you; builds self-control)
- *(do nothing)*

If it works: The doctors let {N} go home after two days, with a leaflet, a bruise and a great deal to think about. / {N} walks out of the hospital into a bright, cold morning and breathes it in.  
If it fails: The doctor's face is serious: there is damage that will take months to heal. / On the third day the questions start: from the family, from work, and from people with forms.

## Outside events, read through the person's own filter

The person does not choose the reading; their colors, mindset and history make one more likely. Impact is how strongly the event's effect lands under that reading.

### your birthday party

daily life · joy · Modern Earth: a cake with candles, a few friends round after school, and a song sung just for the birthday child.

How often: once a year; likelier with a family with a little to spare; friends living close by; rarer with hard times at home; a move just before the day.

- **a day to say thanks: to the guests, the family, and everyone who came** (White reading; impact x0.9; also belonging+.05)  
  *{N} hands out the party bags at the door and thanks every guest by name.*
- **one year older: what is different now, and what comes next?** (Blue reading; impact x0.8)  
  *{N} stands against the kitchen door frame to be measured, and studies the new pencil line for a long time.*
- **presents, and being the centre of everything for a whole day** (Black reading; impact x1.0)  
  *{N} opens every present in front of everyone and keeps careful count.*
- **the best day of the year: cake, games and shouting** (Red reading; impact x1.35)  
  *{N} runs round the garden in a paper crown, high on cake and noise.*
- **the family all together, the same songs and the same cake as every year** (Green reading; impact x1.0)  
  *{N} blows out the candles while {grandparent} sings the old birthday song a beat behind everyone.*

### a week with the grandparents

daily life · joy · Modern Earth: a week of the school holidays at the grandparents' house: their rules, their food, their garden and their stories.

How often: a week every year or two, where grandparents are alive and close enough; likelier with grandparents alive and nearby; parents who both work; rarer with grandparents far away or unwell; hard times at home.

- **proper manners, early nights and an old-fashioned kind of looking after** (White reading; impact x0.9)  
  *{N} lays the table the old way, with the knives and forks just so, and is thanked for it.*
- **old photographs, a shed full of strange tools, and stories about the old days** (Blue reading; impact x1.0; also competence+.05)  
  *{N} spends the afternoon in the shed while {grandparent} explains what each old tool is for.*
- **spoilt rotten: second helpings, later bedtimes and coins pressed into a hand** (Black reading; impact x0.9)  
  *{N} works out quickly that {grandparent} says yes to almost anything, and makes the most of it.*
- **freedom: the woods behind the house, the river and nobody fussing** (Red reading; impact x1.3)  
  *{N} is out in the woods all morning and comes back for lunch muddy to the knees.*
- **slow days in the garden, and being part of something older** (Green reading; impact x1.0)  
  *{N} helps {grandparent} water the tomatoes in the evening, slowly, the way it has always been done.*

How often: once a year; likelier with a town that puts on a display; a dry night; rarer with hard times; rain; a family that keeps away from crowds.

- **the whole town together, safely behind the rope** (White reading; impact x0.9; also belonging+.05)  
  *{N} holds {parent}'s hand tight and stays behind the rope, as everyone was told to.*
- **how do they make the colours, and why does the bang come after the light?** (Blue reading; impact x0.9)  
  *{N} counts the seconds between each flash and its bang, and works out how far away the rockets are.*
- **the biggest sparkler and the best view, for whoever gets to the front** (Black reading; impact x0.8; also autonomy+.05)  
  *{N} wriggles to the front of the crowd for the best view and does not give it up.*
- **bangs, flashes and a sky on fire** (Red reading; impact x1.4)  
  *{N} shrieks at every bang and writes a name in the air with a sparkler, over and over.*
- **the dark, the cold, the smell of smoke, and everyone looking up at once** (Green reading; impact x1.0)

community · joy · Modern Earth: after a season of losing, the under-elevens win their Saturday match, and the parents on the touchline go wild.
